QASHANI:39:5-6/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:5-6/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:5-6/r3.claim: The single self is the universal rational self, the true Adam, from whom the animal self is made as its spouse; visible forms descend from the Preserved Tablet and hidden world.
QASHANI:39:5-6/r3.anchor: هي آدم الحقيقي، أي: النفس الناطقة الكلية، التي تتشعب عنها النفوس الجزئية

QASHANI:39:5-6/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:5-6/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:5-6/r4.claim: The three darknesses are bodily nature, vegetative soul, and animal soul; creation unfolds in stages and produces multiplicity from unity through names, qualities, and acts.
QASHANI:39:5-6/r4.anchor: من الطبيعة الجسمانية والنفس النباتية والحيوانية

QASHANI:39:5-6/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:5-6/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:5-6/r5.claim: God alone possesses real being and sovereignty, so worshipping anything else turns people toward what does not exist independently.
QASHANI:39:5-6/r5.anchor: يتصرف فيه بأفعاله { لا إله إلا هو } في الوجود { فأنى تصرفون } عن عبادته

QUSHAYRI:v3p112/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p112/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p112/r6.claim: God creates people through stages in three darknesses: abdomen, womb, and placenta; recalling this origin should prevent self-admiration.

QUSHAYRI:v3p112/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p112/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p112/r7.claim: Some organs house qualities such as knowledge, power, and life, while others serve the senses.
QUSHAYRI:v3p112/r7.anchor: سخر بعضها محال للصفات الحميدة كالعلم

QUSHAYRI:v3p112/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p112/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p112/r8.claim: These gifts remind people of God, since souls and hearts naturally love their benefactor, drawing them to love Him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p112/r8.anchor: ويقال هذه كلها نعم أنعم الله بها علينا

QUSHAYRI:v3p112/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p112/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p112/r9.claim: God identifies Himself as Creator, Provider, shaper, benefactor, and guide who teaches people His unity and requires them to keep His limits.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r10.claim: Humanity comes from one soul, Adam; the reported account says Eve was created from Adam, making later human creation mediated through Eve.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r10.anchor: وهي آدم عليه السلام، وذلك أن حواء على ما روي خلقت من آدم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r11.claim: Another view has Adam's progeny drawn out like particles before Eve was created, making them descend from Adam without her mediation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r11.anchor: وقيل: أخرج ذرية آدم من ظهره كالذر، ثم خلق بعد ذلك حواء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r12.claim: On the second account, thumma is temporal; on the first, it orders the discourse rather than the actual time of Eve's creation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r12.anchor: وجاءت على هذا القول على وضعها، ثم للمهلة في الزمان، وعلى القول الأول يظهر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says creating Eve from Adam's body was an exceptional sign, so thumma marks its greater rank as a sign rather than later existence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r1.anchor: فكانت أدخل في كونها آية، وأجلب لعجب السامع، فعطفها بثم على الآية الأولى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r2.claim: The livestock are described as “sent down” metaphorically because their destinies were written in the heavenly tablet or their plant food grows from rain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r2.anchor: ووصف الأنعام بالإنزال مجازا ما، لأن قضاياه توصف بالنزول من السماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r3.claim: Poetic usage places camel humps “in his cloud,” supporting cloud as the meaning of rabāb; another poem similarly uses a surprising preposition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r3.anchor: أسنمة الآبال في ربابه أي: في سحابه، وقال آخر: صار الثريد في رؤوس العيدان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r4.claim: Another view says the livestock were created in Paradise and literally sent down, so their origins were descended.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r4.anchor: وقيل: خلقها في الجنة ثم أنزلها، فعلى هذا يكون إنزال أصولها حقيقة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r5.claim: The eight pairs are male and female camels, cattle, sheep, and goats; a pair has another of its kind, whereas alone it is singular.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r5.anchor: والأنعام: الإبل والبقر والضأن والمعز، ثمانية أزواج، لأن كلا منها ذكر وأنثى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r6.claim: The wording about the two sexes is also stated at 75:39.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r6.anchor: وقال تعالى: فجعل منه الزوجين الذكر والأنثى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says successive creation refers to descendants, from Adam and then from their fathers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد: خلقا من بعد خلق: آخر من ظهر آدم وظهور الآباء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r8.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r8.claim: These authorities interpret successive creation as stages such as the morsel, clot, and other embryonic forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r8.anchor: وقال عكرمة ومجاهد والسدي: رتبا خلقا من بعد خلق على المضغة والعلقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari enumerates the sequence as a sound animal after bones covered with flesh, bare bones, morsels, clots, and drops.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r9.anchor: حيوانا سويا، من بعد عظام مكسوة لحما، من بعد عظام عارية، من بعد مضغ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r10.speaker: عيسى وطلحة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r10.claim: They assimilate the qāf into the kāf in yakhluqukum.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r10.anchor: وقرأ عيسى وطلحة: يخلقكم، بإدغام القاف في الكاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r11.claim: The three darknesses are the abdomen, womb, and placenta, or alternatively the loins, womb, and abdomen.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r11.anchor: والظلمات الثلاث: البطن والرحم والمشيمة، وقيل: الصلب والرحم والبطن.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r12.claim: Dhālikum refers back to the creator described in the preceding acts; “how are you turned away?” rebukes turning from His worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p185/r12.anchor: ذلكم: إشارة إلى المتصف بتلك الأوصاف السابقة من خلق السموات

MAJAZ:v2p188/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p188/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p188/r2.claim: One explanation of the three layers of darkness is men's loins, then the womb, then the belly.
MAJAZ:v2p188/r2.anchor: «في ظلمات ثلاث » (6) فى أصلاب الرجال ثم فى الرحم ثم فى البطن

MAJAZ:v2p188/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p188/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p188/r3.claim: Others explain the three as the membrane around the fetus, the womb, and the belly.
MAJAZ:v2p188/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم فى الحولاء وفى الرحم وفى البطن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r5.claim: The single soul is Adam and his mate is Eve.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r5.anchor: يعني: آدم، {ثم جعل منها زوجها} يعني حواء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r6.claim: “Sending down” livestock means creating them; alternatives connect it to water producing cotton and fodder or making livestock provisions.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r6.anchor: معنى الإنزال هاهنا: الإحداث والإنشاء، كقوله تعالى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r7.claim: The eight pairs are species, explained in al-Anʿām.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r7.anchor: ثمانية أزواج} أصناف، تفسيرها في سورة الأنعام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r8.claim: Womb creation proceeds from drop to clot to lump of flesh, as in Noah 14.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r9.claim: The three darknesses are the abdomen, womb, and placenta.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r9.anchor: ظلمة البطن، وظلمة الرحم، وظلمة المشيمة

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r3.claim: Human creation in the lower world is another, nearer and more remarkable proof: Adam without parents, Eve from his rib, then innumerable descendants from both.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r3.anchor: استدلال آخر بما أوجده في العالم السفلي مبدوء به من خلق الإنسان

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r4.claim: ثم may attach to an omitted description of نفس, to the sense of وحدة, or to خلقكم, marking the contrast between ordinary reproduction and the exceptional creation of Eve.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r4.anchor: { ثم } للعطف على محذوف هو صفة { نفس } مثل خلقها أو على معنى واحدة

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r5.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r5.claim: One account says God drew Adam’s descendants from his back like particles, then created Eve from them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r5.anchor: وقيل أخرج من ظهره ذريته كالذر ثم خلق منها حواء

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r6.claim: أنزل لكم means either decreed or apportioned livestock, with divine decisions written in heaven, or brought them about through descending causes such as starlight and rain.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r6.anchor: { وأنزل لكم } وقضى أو قسم لكم، فإن قضاياه وقسمه توصف بالنزول من السماء

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r7.claim: The eight livestock pairs are male and female camels, cattle, sheep, and goats.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r7.anchor: { من الأنعم ثمنية أزوج } ذكر وأنثى من الإبل والبقر والضأن والمعز

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r8.claim: The stages in wombs display extraordinary power: a formed animal follows flesh-covered bones, bare bones, morsels, clots, and drops; the three darknesses are abdomen, womb, and placenta, or loins, womb, and abdomen.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r8.anchor: { خلقا من بعد خلق } حيوانا سويا من بعد عظام مكسوة لحما

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r9.claim: Addressing humans either favors rational beings or singles out the intended audience; God alone owns creation and therefore alone deserves worship, so turning to idolatry is inexplicable.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r9.anchor: إذ لا يشاركه في الخلق غيره

NAHHAS:v4p3/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p3/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p3/r10.claim: The darkness does not prevent the sun or moon as it prevents created beings.
NAHHAS:v4p3/r10.anchor: أي لا تمنعه الظلمة كما تمنع المخلوقين

BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r7.claim: The creation of animals and especially humans, with speech and inescapable bodily conditions, is a further sign of divine oneness and power; humanity comes from Adam, a single soul.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r7.anchor: { من نفس واحدة } هي آدم عليه السلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p330/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p330/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p330/r3.claim: The discourse turns to the remarkable creation of humanity, including the single original soul and Adam's spouse, whose creation enables procreation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p330/r3.anchor: انتقال إلى الاستدلال بخلق الناس وهو الخلق العجيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p330/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p330/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p330/r4.claim: The human-creation clause may be circumstantial from the mention of God or a fresh, repeated proof; its address to polytheists shifts from third to second person for indirect and direct argument together.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p330/r4.anchor: والخطاب للمشركين بدليل قوله بعده : { فأنى تصرفون } ، وهو التفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p330/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p330/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p330/r5.claim: Then marks rank, not chronology: creating Adam's spouse from himself is an independent and more astonishing proof than the creation of descendants, unlike the blessing-focused sequence in 7:189.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p330/r5.anchor: لأن زمن خلق زوج آدم سابق على خلق الناس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86/r3.claim: Human groups differ in kind, language, and color while descending from Adam and his wife Eve, as also stated in 4:1.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86/r3.anchor: خلقكم مع اختلاف أجناسكم وأصنافكم وألسنتكم وألوانكم من نفس واحدة، وهو آدم عليه السلام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86#2/r1.claim: The eight livestock pairs are created for people from the animals' offspring: two each from sheep, goats, camels, and cattle, as listed in 6:143–144.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86#2/r1.anchor: من ظهور الأنعام ثمانية، أزواج وهي المذكورة في سورة الأنعام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86#2/r2.claim: In the womb, a person develops from sperm to clot, then lump, flesh, bones, sinews, and veins, receives a spirit, and becomes a new creation, as in 23:14.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86#2/r2.anchor: أي: يكون أحدكم أولا نطفة، ثم يكون علقة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة وأبو مالك والضحاك وقتادة والسدي وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86#2/r3.claim: The three darknesses are the womb, the placenta or protective covering, and the abdomen, according to Ibn ʿAbbās and the listed early authorities.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وعكرمة، وأبو مالك، والضحاك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86#3/r1.claim: The creator of the heavens, earth, people, and their ancestors is their Lord, sovereign and controller; only He deserves worship, so worshipping another is irrational diversion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86#3/r1.anchor: هو الرب له الملك والتصرف (8) في جميع ذلك

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r5.claim: The one soul is Adam and the spouse made from it is Eve.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r5.anchor: يعني من آدم . { ثم جعل منها زوجها } يعني حواء

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r6.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r6.claim: Eve was created from a rib on Adam's back, below the ribs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r6.anchor: أنه خلقها من ضلع الخلف من آدم وهو أسفل الأضلاع

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r7.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r7.claim: Alternatively, she was created from Adam's substance; from her means like her.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r7.anchor: أنه خلقها من مثل ما خلق منه آدم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r8.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r8.claim: The eight pairs are two each of camels, cattle, sheep, and goats.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r8.anchor: قال قتادة : من الإبل اثنين , ومن البقر اثنين

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r9.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r9.claim: Anzala means God made the livestock for people.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r10.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r10.claim: Alternatively, God sent the livestock down after creating them in Paradise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r10.anchor: أنزلها بعد أن خلقها في الجنة , حكاه ابن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r11.speaker: قتادة والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r11.claim: Creation after creation means sperm, clot, morsel, bones, then flesh.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r11.anchor: نطفة ثم علقة ثم مضغة ثم عظاما ثم لحما , قاله قتادة والسدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r12.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r12.claim: Alternatively, creation in wombs follows creation in Adam's loins.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r12.anchor: خلقا في بطون أمهاتكم من بعد خلقكم في ظهرآدم , قاله السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r13.claim: A further possibility is creation in the father's loins, mother's womb, then after birth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r13.anchor: خلقا في ظهر الأب ثم خلقا في بطن الأم ثم خلقا بعد الوضع

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة ومجاهد وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r14.claim: The three darknesses are abdomen, womb, and placenta.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r14.anchor: ظلمة البطن وظلمة الرحم وظلمة المشيمة ، قاله ابن عباس وعكرمة ومجاهد وقتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r15.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r15.claim: Alternatively, they are the man's loins, woman's belly, and womb.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r15.anchor: ظلمة صلب الرجل وظلمة بطن المرأة وظلمة الرحم ، حكاه ابن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r16.claim: A further reading invokes night surrounding darknesses of placenta, inner parts, and belly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r16.anchor: ظلمة عتمة الليل التي تحيط بظلمة المشيمة مظلمة الأحشاء

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r10.claim: The one soul is Adam, and God made his spouse from him so that procreation could occur.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r10.anchor: { خلقكم من نفس واحدة } يعني آدم عليه السلام { ثم جعل منها زوجها } يعني ليحصل التناسل

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r11.claim: The livestock are described as sent down because plants grew from water sent down; this is a staged causal expression, like clothing being sent down.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r11.anchor: أخبر عن الأزواج بالنزول، لأنها تكونت بالنبات والنبات بالماء المنزل. وهذا يسمى التدريج ومثله قوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r1.claim: Sent down can mean brought into being; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr specifically glosses it as created.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r1.anchor: وقيل: أنزل أنشأ وجعل. وقال سعيد بن جبير: خلق.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r2.claim: Another view says God created the livestock in Paradise and sent them down to earth, analogously to the iron sent with Adam.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: إن الله تعالى خلق هذه الأنعام في الجنة ثم أنزلها إلى الأرض كما قيل في قوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r3.claim: The phrase can mean that God gave these animals to people.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: «وأنزل لكم من الأنعام» أي أعطاكم.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r4.claim: Creation may be called sending down because creation occurs by a command descending from heaven.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: جعل الخلق إنزالا لأن الخلق إنما يكون بأمر ينزل من السماء.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r5.claim: The eight pairs comprise two camels, two cattle, two sheep, and two goats.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r5.anchor: قال قتادة: من الإبل اثنين ومن البقر اثنين ومن الضأن اثنين ومن المعز اثنين كل واحد زوج.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r6.speaker: قتادة والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r6.claim: The successive womb creations are a drop, a clot, a lump, bones, and then flesh.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r6.anchor: قال قتادة والسدي: نطفة ثم علقة ثم مضغة ثم عظما ثم لحما.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r7.claim: He takes the successive creation to begin in Adam's back before creation in the womb.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r7.anchor: ابن زيد: «خلقا من بعد خلق» خلقا في بطون أمهاتكم من بعد خلقكم في ظهر آدم.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r8.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r8.claim: Another interpretation has creation in the father's back, then the mother's womb, and then after birth.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: في ظهر الأب ثم خلقا في بطن الأم ثم خلقا بعد الوضع. ذكره الماوردي.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r9.claim: They identify the three darknesses as the belly, womb, and placenta; Qurtubi says this is the sounder view.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r9.anchor: { في ظلمات ثلاث } ظلمة البطن وظلمة الرحم وظلمة المشيمة. قاله ابن عباس وعكرمة ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r10.speaker: ابن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r10.claim: He identifies the three darknesses as the placenta, womb, and night.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r10.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: ظلمة المشيمة وظلمة الرحم وظلمة الليل.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r11.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r11.claim: He identifies them as the man's loins, the woman's belly, and the womb; none of these veils anything from God.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r11.anchor: وهذا مذهب أبي عبيدة. أي لا تمنعه الظلمة كما تمنع المخلوقين.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r12.claim: The creator of these things is the Lord and king, the only deity; the question asks how people turn from worshipping Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r12.anchor: { ذلكم الله } أي الذي خلق هذه الأشياء { ربكم له الملك لا إله إلا هو }. { فأنى تصرفون } أي كيف تنقلبون وتنصرفون عن عبادته

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r13.speaker: حمزة
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r13.claim: Hamza reads the word for mothers with kasra on both hamza and mīm.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r14.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r14.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads it with kasra on hamza and fatḥa on mīm; the remaining readers use ḍamma and fatḥa.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6#2/r14.anchor: والكسائي بكسر الهمزة وفتح الميم. الباقون بضم الهمزة وفتح الميم.

ZAJJAJ:v4p344/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p344/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p344/r4.claim: ثم marks sequence: the one soul is Adam and his spouse Eve, made from him before the rest of humankind.
ZAJJAJ:v4p344/r4.anchor: والنفس الواحدة يعني بها آدم - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وزوجها حواء.

RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r1.claim: “His is the dominion” is exclusive: if another god had power, the two would conflict, which is impossible; if it had none, it would be deficient, so only God is deity and worthy of worship.
RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r1.anchor: وهذا يفيد الحصر أي له الملك لا لغيره

RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r4.claim: God's charge does not seek benefit or avert harm for Him; as the necessary existent in His essence and attributes, He is absolutely self-sufficient.
RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r4.anchor: إن الله تعالى ما كلف المكلفين ليجر إلى نفسه منفعة أو ليدفع عن نفسه مضرة

RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r5.claim: If God needed something eternally, it would require creation in eternity, a contradiction; if the need arose later, it would be a deficiency no wise being seeks.
RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r5.anchor: والأول باطل وإلا لزم أن يخلق في الأزل ما كان محتاجا إليه وذلك محال

RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r6.claim: Regardless of whether appetite or need can be attributed to God, it is necessarily known that the creator of the heavens and all creatures cannot benefit from one person's prayer or be harmed by its absence; all worlds' disbelief cannot harm Him.
RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r6.anchor: من المعلوم بالضرورة أن الإله القادر على خلق السموات

TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r1.claim: Both verses establish exclusive lordship by joining creation and governance: pagans accept one Creator but multiply lords, while governance remains part of creation.
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r1.anchor: وقد جمع فيهما بين الخلق والتدبير لما مر مرارا أن إثبات وحدة الخالق

TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r7.claim: The one soul is Adam, and his mate is a woman of the same human kind; humanity multiplied from the two, with then marking rhetorical sequence.
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r7.anchor: والمراد بزوجها امرأته التي هي من نوعها وتماثلها في الإنسانية

TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r8.claim: The eight livestock pairs are camels, cattle, sheep, and goats, each counted as male and female.
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r8.anchor: وكونها ثمانية أزواج باعتبار انقسامها إلى الذكر والأنثى

TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r9.claim: Calling the livestock sent down describes their appearance in the visible world as descent from God's unseen treasuries.
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r9.anchor: تسمية خلق للأنعام إنزالا لها باعتبار أنه تعالى يسمي ظهور الأشياء في الكون بعد ما لم يكن إنزالا لها

THALABI:v8p221#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p221#3/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p221#3/r6.claim: The eight pairs of livestock are kinds and individual animals; the creation in the womb proceeds through sperm, clinging clot, then lump of flesh.
THALABI:v8p221#3/r6.anchor: أصناف وأفراد، تفسيرها في سورة الأنعام

THALABI:v8p221#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p221#3/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v8p221#3/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the successive creation in the womb to mean creation after the first creation in Adam's back.
THALABI:v8p221#3/r7.anchor: معناه يخلقكم في بطون أمهاتكم من بعد الخلق الأول الذي خلقكم في ظهر آدم

THALABI:v8p221#3/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p221#3/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p221#3/r8.claim: The three darknesses are the abdomen, womb, and placenta.
THALABI:v8p221#3/r8.anchor: في ظلمات ثلاث يعني البطن والرحم والمشيمة

ELMALILI:39:3-9/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:3-9/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:3-9/r5.claim: The three darknesses are the darkness of the abdomen, the womb, and the placenta.
ELMALILI:39:3-9/r5.anchor: Üç zulmette batın zulmeti, rahim zulmeti

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r9.claim: Humanity's descent from Adam is as wondrous as the universe's formation and operation, carrying wisdom that leads reflective hearts to prostrate before divine power.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r9.anchor: İnsanlık âleminin bir tek candan, Âdem’den gelişi de evrenin oluşu ve işleyişi kadar muhteşem bir olaydır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r10.claim: The verse succinctly alludes both to humanity's formation and to each person's development in the womb.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r10.anchor: Âyet, bütünüyle insanlığın bu oluş süreci yanında her bir insanın ana rahmindeki yaratılış sürecine de veciz bir üslûpla değinmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r11.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r11.claim: The three darknesses are commonly explained as the abdominal wall, uterine wall, and darkness of the membrane surrounding the fetus.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r11.anchor: Müfessirler, “üç karanlık” tabirini, annenin karın duvarı, rahim duvarı ve cenini kuşatan zar (amnion zarı) içindeki karanlık tabakalar olarak açıklarlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r12.claim: Alternatively, the three layers can be understood as the amnion, chorion, and decidua membranes, which protect or nourish the fetus.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r12.anchor: Bunların ilki, cenini koruyan, içi sıvı dolu amnion zarı, ikincisi amnionu dıştan kuşatan ve daha çok ceninin besin ve oksijen almasını sağlayan korion zarıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r13.claim: Mentioning darkness emphasizes that even hidden events in the womb occur through God's knowledge and power, producing wonders unseen from outside.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r13.anchor: bu karanlık ortamlarda olup bitenlerin dahi Allah’ın bilgisi ve kudreti sayesinde gerçekleştiğine

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r14.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r14.claim: The stages include nutfah, alaqah, mudghah, and subsequent development described in Hajj and the Believers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r14.anchor: Hac (22/5) ve Mü’minûn (23/12-14) sûrelerinde açılımı verilen nutfe, alaka ve mudga safhalarının

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r15.claim: The commentary explains the embryonic sequence: fertilized cell, attachment to the uterine wall, a morsel-like embryo, then bones covered by muscles, vessels, and nerves.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r15.anchor: Rahim karanlığında döllenmiş hücreye (zigot) nutfe, hücrenin rahim cidarındaki asılı vaziyetine alaka denir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r16.claim: The eight animal pairs are male and female sheep, goats, camels, and cattle.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r16.anchor: koyun, keçi, deve ve sığır çiftleridir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r2.claim: People depend on God, return to Him, and face individual judgment; He knows every deed and hidden secret.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r2.anchor: everyone is destined to return to God; on that Day, no one will bear the burden of any other person

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p527/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p527/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p527/r3.claim: God created every human from one soul and made its mate from the same species; since God alone creates, no other being can be Lord.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p527/r3.anchor: it is God Who has created every one from a single soul, and then created its mate from the same species.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p527/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p527/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p527/r4.claim: God alone creates, provides for creatures, and knows all things, so people have no basis for assigning lordship to partners.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p527/r4.anchor: when God is the Creator and He alone has set up this whole system of providence for His creatures

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p528/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p528/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p528/r1.claim: God created livestock as humanity's livelihood and sustenance; the wording 'sent down' like 57:25 points people beyond immediate causes to God, the true source, and fosters gratitude.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p528/r1.anchor: it is God Who sends down all things. He sent down iron and as a result it was produced in the earth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p528/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p528/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p528/r2.claim: Zawj can mean a pair or one member of it; here it denotes individual male and female animals, eight kinds among four familiar domestic species central to Arab livelihoods.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p528/r2.anchor: Here, it is used in this latter meaning. In Arabia, four types of domestic cattle were very common

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p528/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p528/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p528/r3.claim: The detailed stages of fetal development in three layers of darkness demonstrate God's creative skill and all-embracing knowledge.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p528/r3.anchor: It is said that it is God Who makes the foetus pass through various phases of creation in the wombs of mothers in three layers darkness.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p529/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p529/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p529/r1.claim: The three darknesses are the membrane, womb, and cavity enclosing the womb; God's skill works unseen in darkness, proving His comprehensive knowledge.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p529/r1.anchor: The three layers of darkness refer to the membrane, the womb and the hollow in which the womb is enclosed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p529/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p529/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p529/r2.claim: The passive 'where are you turned away?' implies that despite clear evidence people surrender their reins to a devil who leads them from truth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p529/r2.anchor: they have consigned their reigns to some devil who is leading them into darkness and taking them away from the truth.

JISHUMI:v8p6043/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r12.claim: God's creation and shaping in the womb, and the creation of Adam from soil and Eve from Adam's rib, demonstrate perfect power and knowledge; perception through an instrument could not operate in the womb.
JISHUMI:v8p6043/r12.anchor: أما الأول: فخلقه وتصويره في الرحم، وخلق آدم من تراب، وخلق حواء من ضلعه

TABRISI:39:6-10/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:6-10/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:6-10/r6.claim: In “that is God, your Lord,” “that” is a subject, “God” an explanatory apposition, and “your Lord” a substitute or predicate.
TABRISI:39:6-10/r6.anchor: ذلكم مبتدأ والله عطف بيان وربكم بدل من لفظة الله

TABRISI:39:6-10/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:6-10/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:6-10/r7.claim: “To Him belongs sovereignty” may be circumstantial, with sovereignty raised by the adverb, or may be a second predicate.
TABRISI:39:6-10/r7.anchor: له الملك يرتفع الملك بالظرف والظرف مع ما ارتفع به في موضع الحال

TABRISI:39:6-10/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:6-10/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:6-10/r8.claim: The clause “there is no deity but Him” may be circumstantial, meaning uniquely one, or another predicate.
TABRISI:39:6-10/r8.anchor: جاز أن يكون في موضع الحال أي متوحدا بالوحدانية وجاز أن يكون خبرا آخر

TABRISI:39:6-10/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:6-10/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:6-10/r9.claim: “How are you turned away?” is parsed as a circumstantial accusative or verbal noun and means “how.”
TABRISI:39:6-10/r9.anchor: فأنى تصرفون أنى في موضع نصب على الحال أو على المصدر

TABRISI:39:6-10/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:6-10/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:6-10/r10.claim: The single soul is Adam, from whose line all humanity descends; his spouse is Eve.
TABRISI:39:6-10/r10.anchor: يعني آدم ع لأن جميع البشر من نسله

TABRISI:39:6-10/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:6-10/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:6-10/r11.claim: Eve was made from the surplus of Adam's clay; another view says she came from one of his ribs.
TABRISI:39:6-10/r11.anchor: يعني حواء أي من فضل طينته. وقيل: من ضلع من أضلاعه

TABRISI:39:6-10/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:6-10/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:6-10/r12.claim: One explanation takes “then” as ordinary sequence in the wording even though the second event actually preceded the first; a poem supplies a parallel.
TABRISI:39:6-10/r12.anchor: أنه عطف يوجب أن الكلام الثاني بعد الأول ويجري مجرى قول القائل

TABRISI:39:6-10/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:6-10/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:6-10/r13.claim: A second explanation coordinates to the meaning: God created one soul alone and then made its spouse from it.
TABRISI:39:6-10/r13.anchor: أنه معطوف على معنى واحد فكأنه قال خلقكم من نفس واحدة أوجدها وحدها

TABRISI:39:6-10/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:6-10/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:6-10/r14.claim: A third view says descendants were created as tiny beings from Adam's back before Eve was made from his rib; the author calls this weak.
TABRISI:39:6-10/r14.anchor: وثالثها: أنه خلق الذرية في ظهر آدم وأخرجها من ظهره كالذر

TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r1.claim: “Sent down” the livestock can mean brought into being, like clothing, which comes through rain and the plants it produces.
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r1.anchor: وقد أنزلنا عليكم لباسا [الأعراف: 26] ولم ينزل اللباس

TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r2.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r2.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says livestock were sent down after being created in Paradise; a report says sheep and camels are animals of Paradise.
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r2.anchor: عن الجبائي. قال: وفي الخبر الشاة من دواب الجنة والإبل من دواب الجنة

TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, “sent down” means provided as sustenance; the eight pairs are camels, cattle, sheep, and goats, male and female of each, as explained in al-Anʿām.
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r3.anchor: أن المعنى جعلها نزلا ورزقا لكم ويعني بالأزواج الثمانية من الأنعام الإبل

TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r4.speaker: قتادة، مجاهد، السدي
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r4.claim: Creation in the womb passes through stages: drop, clot, lump, bones, flesh clothing the bones, then a further creation.
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r4.anchor: نطفة ثم علقة ثم مضغة ثم عظاما ثم يكسو العظام لحما

TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd understands the womb's successive creation as following the earlier creation in Adam's back.
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r5.anchor: بعد الخلق في ظهر آدم عن ابن زيد

TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة، السدي، ابن زيد
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r6.claim: The three darknesses are those of the abdomen, womb, and placenta; the interpretation is also transmitted from Abu Jaʿfar.
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r6.anchor: ظلمة البطن وظلمة الرحم وظلمة المشيمة عن ابن عباس ومجاهد

TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r7.claim: Another explanation counts night, the man's loins, the womb, and the abdomen among the darknesses.
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r7.anchor: ظلمة الليل أو ظلمة صلب الرجل وظلمة الرحم وظلمة البطن

TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r8.claim: God created these things, owns sovereignty over all creatures, and alone is deity; after this proof, turning away from truth is inexplicable.
TABRISI:39:6-10#2/r8.anchor: الذي خلق هذه الأشياء { ربكم } الذي يملك التصرف فيكم

ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n7/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n7/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n7/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to 4:1 and its note for the parallel discussion of the first human pair.

ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n8/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n8/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n8/r1.claim: The eight pairs are male and female animals from four kinds: sheep, goats, camels, and bovines.
ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n8/r1.anchor: the male and the female of four kinds of cattle (sheep, goats, camels and bovine cattle)

ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n8/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n8/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n8/r2.claim: Unlike the same cattle in 6:143–144, where they figure in baseless pre-Islamic taboos, here they are God's lawful gift.
ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n8/r2.anchor: meaningless, superstitious taboos of pre-Islamic times

ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n8/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n8/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n8/r3.claim: Their mention reminds people that God supplies their sustenance and that they depend entirely on Him.
ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n8/r3.anchor: God who provides his sustenance and that, therefore, man is utterly dependent on Him

ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n9/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n9/r1.claim: The three darknesses denote the womb, the membrane around the embryo, and prenatal blindness; embryonic stages are repeatedly mentioned in the Qur'an.
ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n9/r1.anchor: the darkness of the womb, the membrane enveloping the embryo, and its pre-natal blindness

ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n10/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n10/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n10/r1.claim: The closing question literally asks how people are turned away, meaning turned away from the truth.
ASAD-NOTES:39:6#n10/r1.anchor: Lit., "how, then, are you turned away?" - i.e., from the truth.

BURSEVI:v8p55/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p55/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p55/r1.claim: The one soul is Adam; Eve was made either from Adam’s kind or from his short rib, identified as the rib near the flank or the last rib. The omitted clause avoids implying that Eve was created after Adam’s offspring.
BURSEVI:v8p55/r1.anchor: وهي الضلع التي تلي الخاصرة ، أو هي آخر الأضلاع

BURSEVI:v8p55/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p55/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p55/r2.claim: An inward reading takes the single soul as the spirit and its spouse as the heart, created from it as Eve was from Adam’s rib; God alone creates, so He should be worshipped without association.
BURSEVI:v8p55/r2.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن الله تعالى خلق الإنسان من نفس واحدة هي الروح

BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r1.claim: “Sent down” may mean decreed and apportioned, written in the Preserved Tablet, or brought about through heavenly causes such as rain and starlight.
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r1.anchor: أي : قضى وقسم لكم ، فإن قضاياه تعالى وقسمه

BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r2.claim: As with the clothing verse, God sends the water that produces cotton and wool rather than the clothing itself.
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r2.anchor: وهذا كقوله : قد أنزلنا عليكم لباسا ، ولم ينزل اللباس نفسه

BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r3.claim: The eight livestock pairs are male and female camels, cattle, sheep, and goats; anʿām originally denotes a group of camels and has no singular of that form.
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r3.anchor: ذكرا وأنثى ، هي الإبل والبقر والضأن والمعز والأنعام جمع نعم

BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r4.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh restricts anʿām to four kinds, yielding eight pairs because each species’ male and female form a pair; horses, mules, and donkeys are excluded.
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ في أول المائدة : الأنعام مخصوص بالأنواع الأربعة

BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r5.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r5.claim: Al-Baḥr explains that each of two things of the same kind is a pair, while in arithmetic “even” contrasts with “odd.”
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r5.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" الواحد إذا كان وحده ، فهو فرد

BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r6.claim: These four animal types are singled out because people benefit from their meat, hides, hair, and wool.
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r6.anchor: وخصصت هذه الأنواع الأربعة بالذكر لكثرة الانتفاع بها من اللحم والجلد والشعر والوبر

BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r7.claim: An inward reading interprets the eight livestock pairs as eight animal traits in humans: eating, drinking, excretion, urination, desire, greed, rapacity, and anger.
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r7.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : وأنزل لكم من الأنعام ثمانية أزواج

BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r8.claim: The traits reduce to desire and anger, which every animal needs to survive: desire attracts benefits, and anger repels harms.
BURSEVI:v8p55#2/r8.anchor: وأصل جميع هذه الصفات الصفتان الاثنتان : الشهوة والغضب

BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r1.claim: The plural ummahāt means mothers and adds hāʾ to umm, as ahraqa adds hāʾ to araqa.
BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r1.anchor: أي : في أرحامهن جمع أم زيدت الهاء فيه كما زيدت

BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r2.claim: Creation proceeds in stages: a living, proportioned being develops from bones covered with flesh, bare bones, formed and unformed mors, a clot, and a drop of semen.
BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r2.anchor: أي : خلقا مدرجا حيوانا سويا من بعد عظام مكسوة لحما

BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r3.claim: The three darknesses are the abdomen, womb, and placenta, the thin membrane surrounding the fetus; another account lists the loins, abdomen, and womb.
BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r3.anchor: وهي ظلمة البطن وظلمة الرحم وظلمة المشيمة ، وهي بالفتح محل الولد

BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r4.claim: An inward reading calls the three darknesses the darkness of created nature, of the spirit’s existence, and of human nature, or body, nature, and self.
BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r4.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى ظلمة الخلقية وظلمة وجود الروح وظلمة البشرية

BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r5.claim: As a fetus emerges at birth from physical darkness into the visible world, the spiritual seeker’s second birth leads from these darknesses into the unseen world of the heart and spirit.
BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r5.anchor: فكما أن الجنين يخرج في الولادة الأولى من الظلمات المذكورة إلى نور عالم الملك والشهادة

BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r6.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r6.claim: Hafez’s couplet urges the soul to spread its wings and call from the Tree of Ṭūbā rather than remain imprisoned in its cage.
BURSEVI:v8p55#3/r6.anchor:
قال الحافظ :
بال بكشا وصفير از شجر طوبى زن

BURSEVI:v8p56/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p56/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p56/r1.claim: God alone holds unrestricted sovereignty in this life and the next; no one shares it in any respect.
BURSEVI:v8p56/r1.anchor: على الإطلاق في الدنيا والآخرة ليس لغيره شركة في ذلك بوجه من الوجوه

BURSEVI:v8p56/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p56/r2.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v8p56/r2.claim: A great Sufi says divine sovereignty includes power to bring servants to exalted stations and gifts, so they should not despair because God is able.
BURSEVI:v8p56/r2.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : له ملك القدرة على تبليغ العباد إلى المقامات العلية والكرامات السنية

BURSEVI:v8p56/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p56/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p56/r3.claim: The declaration that none is God means none deserves worship or is the true goal; ultimately God alone is absolute existence and essential unity.
BURSEVI:v8p56/r3.anchor: فهو الوجود المطلق والهوية المطلقة والواحدة الذاتية

BURSEVI:v8p56/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p56/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p56/r4.claim: The verse rebukes turning from servitude to God toward powerless creatures and idols, despite abundant reasons to worship God and no sound motive for worshipping others.
BURSEVI:v8p56/r4.anchor: فكيف ، ومن أي وجه تصرفون وتردون عن ملازمة بابه بالعبودية إلى باب عاجز مثلكم من الخلق

BURSEVI:v8p56/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p56/r5.speaker: علي كرم الله وجهه
BURSEVI:v8p56/r5.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet said he had never worshipped an idol or drunk wine.
BURSEVI:v8p56/r5.anchor: قال علي كرم الله وجهه : قيل للنبي عليه السلام : هل عبدت وثنا قط. قال : لا ، قيل : هل شربت خمرا. قال : لا

BURSEVI:v8p56/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p56/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p56/r6.claim: Rational proofs alone suffice to invalidate worship of anything besides God; revelation reinforces them, and God alone merits servitude as creator and true benefactor.
BURSEVI:v8p56/r6.anchor: فأدلة العقل وحدها كافية في الحكم ببطلان عبادة غير الله ، فكيف وقد انضم إليها أدلة الشرع

BURSEVI:v8p56/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p56/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد الخراز قدس سره
BURSEVI:v8p56/r7.claim: Al-Kharraz defines servitude through truthful fidelity, following the Messenger in religious law, and sincere counsel to the community.
BURSEVI:v8p56/r7.anchor: قال أبو سعيد الخراز قدس سره : العبودية ثلاثة : الوفاءعلى الحقيقة ومتابعة الرسول في الشريعة

BURSEVI:v8p56/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p56/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p56/r8.claim: Worship is the purpose for which beings were created, whether understood as knowledge or otherwise, since true knowledge arises only through worship.
BURSEVI:v8p56/r8.anchor: كما قال الله تعالى : {وما خلقت الجن والانس إلا ليعبدون} (الذاريات : 56) سواء فسرت العبادة بالمعرفة أم لا

BURSEVI:v8p56/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p56/r9.speaker: معاذ رضي الله عنه
BURSEVI:v8p56/r9.claim: The excerpt begins Muadh's question to the Prophet about an act that would admit him to Paradise and keep him far from Hell.
BURSEVI:v8p56/r9.anchor: وعن معاذ رضي الله عنه ، قال : قلت : يا رسول الله أخبرني بعمل يدخلني الحنة ويباعدني من النار.

QIRAAT-ER:39:6:19#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:39:6:19#1/r1.speaker: author

QIRAAT-ER:39:6:19#1/r1.anchor: Canonical vowel variant with kasrah/imālah-like vocal texture in the initial syllable; no root change

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p171#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p171#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p171#3/r1.claim: Qatadah identifies the eight pairs as two each of sheep, goats, camels, and cattle.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p171#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ثمانية أزواج ﴾ قال من الضأن اثنين ومن المعز اثنين ومن الإبل اثنين ومن البقر اثنين

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p171#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p171#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p171#3/r2.claim: Qatadah identifies the three layers of darkness as the placenta, womb, and abdomen.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p171#3/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ظلمات ثلاث ﴾ قال ظلمة المشيمة وظلمة الرحم وظلمة البطن

ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r1.claim: The creation of humanity is an independent proof of God's oneness and dominion, especially relevant to the lower world; humanity is mentioned first because reason and the divine trust make its creation especially remarkable.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r1.anchor: الخ دليل آخر على الوحدة والقهر وترك عطفه على ( خلق السماوات ) للإيذان باستقلاله في الدلالة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r2.claim: An anonymous saying calls a human a small body containing the greater world, underscoring why human creation is singled out.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r2.anchor: حتى قيل : وتزعم أنك جرم صغير وفيك انطوى العالم الأكبر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r3.claim: The one soul is Adam, and its spouse is Eve; she was created from his lowest left rib, whether from part or all of it, with a replacement created for Adam.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r3.anchor: والمراد بالنفس آدم عليه السلام وقوله تعالى : ( ثم جعل منها زوجها أي حواء

ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r4.claim: Grammatically, “then He made from it its mate” may continue the description of the single soul, or coordinate with “one,” originally a derived noun that can take a verb as its coordinate.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r4.anchor: على معنى أنها خلقت من بعضها أو خلقت منها كلها وخلق الله تعالى لآدم مكانها عطف على محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r5.claim: A further grammatical option coordinates the clause with “your creation”; on this reading, making Eve is a distinct sign more amazing than creating Adam, which explains the verb “made,” and “then” marks rank rather than time.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r5.anchor: أو على ( خلقكم ) لتفاوت ما بينهما في الدلالة فإنهما وإن كانتا آيتين دالتين على ما مر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r6.claim: One view says Adam's descendants were first drawn from his back as particles, so “created you from it” refers to their extraction and “then” is temporal; al-Ālūsī accepts this only if soundly transmitted as Prophetic or equivalent.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r6.anchor: وقيل إنه تعالى أخرج ذرية آدم عليه السلام من ظهره كالذر ثم خلق منه حواء

ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r7.claim: The passage contains three signs: Adam's creation without parents, Eve's creation from Adam's rib, and the countless number of Adam's descendants.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r7.anchor: وقد تضمنت الآية ثلاث آيات خلق آدم عليه السلام بلا أب وأم وخلق حواء من قصيراه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r8.claim: The eight livestock pairs offer another proof from the lower world; “sent down” can figuratively mean God's decree and apportionment, fixed in the Preserved Tablet and conveyed by appointed angels, with the relation of descent to emergence after concealment.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r8.anchor: استدلال بنوع آخر من العالم السفلي والإنزال مجاز عن القضاء والقسمة فإنه تعالى إذا قضى وقسم أثبت ذلك في اللوح المحفوظ

ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r9.claim: Another figurative reading assigns the descent to the livestock while the actual things sent down are causes of their life, such as rain; the relation is association between them.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التجوز في نسبة الإنزال إلى الأنعام والمنزل حقيقة أسباب حياتها كالأمطار

ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r10.claim: Interpretations that take the pairs as the causes of livestock's sustenance, or make their descent mean their production through heavenly causes, are dismissed as unconvincing.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r10.anchor: وقيل يراد بالأزواج أسباب تعيشها أو يجعل الإنزال مجازا عن إحداث ذلك بأسباب سماوية وهو كما ترى

ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r11.claim: A report that God literally created livestock in Paradise and sent them down is mentioned, but al-Ālūsī sees no sound basis for it.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r11.anchor: وقيل الكلام على ظاهره والله تعالى خلق الأنعام في الجنة ثم أنزلها منها ولا أرى لهذا الخبر صحة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r12.claim: The livestock are camels, cattle, sheep, and goats; the eight pairs are the male and female of each kind.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r12.anchor: والأنعام الإبل والبقر والضأن والمعز وكانت ثمانية أزواج لأن كلا منها ذكر وأنثى

ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r13.claim: The adverbial phrase is placed before the explicit object to foreground what precedes and create anticipation for what follows.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p240/r13.anchor: وتقديم الظرفين على المفعول الصريح لما مر مرارا من الإعتناء بما قدم والتشويق إلى ما أخر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p241/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p241/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p241/r1.claim: The concluding question follows from the divine attributes just described: with abundant reasons to worship God, no reason to turn away, and many deterrents to worshiping another, how can people be diverted?
ALUSI-FULL:v23p241/r1.anchor: أي فكيف تصوفون عن عبادته تعالى مع وفور موجباتها ودواعيها وانتفاء الصارف عنها بالكلية

ALUSI-FULL:v24p37#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p37#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v24p37#2/r5.claim: The three darknesses symbolize possibility, prime matter, and form.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p37#2/r5.anchor: قيل : يشير إلى ظلمة الإمكان وظلمة الهيولي وظلمة الصورة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r1.claim: One possible reading takes Eve's creation from Adam's side after his division; ثم marks delay in time and rank, and جعل identifies the male as her cause and material, excluding partnership.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r1.anchor: ولما كان إيجادنا منها بعد شق الأنثى منها , قال عاطفا على ما تقديره : أوجدها من تراب

BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r2.claim: In this reading, Adam was created as the source of the descendants through whom God's perfect attributes would be manifested.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r2.anchor: أنه ما خلق آدم عليه السلام إلا ليكون سببا لما يحدث عنه من الذرية

BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r3.claim: The preferable reading is that God determined all descendants' numbers, colors, and forms when creating Adam, including Eve's descent from him; thus all ultimately originate from Adam.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r3.anchor: ويجوز - وهو أحسن - أن يكون المعنى لأن السياق لإحاطة العلم المدلول عليه بإنزال الكتاب

BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r4.claim: A report from Abu al-Darda says God extracted Adam's descendants from his right shoulder as tiny white ants and from his left as black as charcoal, assigning the right-hand group to Paradise and the left-hand group to Hell.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r4.anchor: في مسند أحمد بن منيع عن أبي الدرداء رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r5.claim: The livestock are described as sent down because their strength surpasses human strength, so their creation and domestication display divine power and human subjugation of them.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r5.anchor: وكان سبحانه موصوفا بالعلو , وكان أكثر الأنعام أشد الإنسان , فكان تسخيره له وتذليله إنزالا عن قوته

BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r6.claim: The eight pairs are camels, cattle, sheep, and goats, each male and female; animals familiar to Arabs are listed, while Bactrian camels and buffaloes are omitted.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r6.anchor: ولما لم يكن عند العرب البخاتي والجواميس لم يذكرها سبحانه , واقتصر على ما عندهم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r7.claim: A pair is one member with another needed for full benefit; unlike humans whose mate comes from the first soul, male and female livestock were each created independently, displaying God's freedom of action.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r7.anchor: وإذا نظرت هذه العبارة مع العبارة عن خلق الإنسان فهمت أن الأنعام خلق كل ذكرها وأناثها على انفراده , لا أن أحدا منها من صاحبه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r8.claim: Creation in the womb unfolds in stages from mixed elements; the three darknesses can be sperm, clot, and lump, with sex becoming known when bones are clothed with flesh.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r8.anchor: ظلمة النطفة ثم العلقة ثم المضغة , فإذا صار عظاما مكسوة لحما عرف هل هو ذكر أو أنثى

BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r9.speaker: عيسى ابن مريم عليه السلام
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r9.claim: An alternate gloss takes the three darknesses as the abdomen, womb, and placenta; Ibn Abbas transmits this view, and Ibn Abi al-Dunya's Book of Contentment attributes it to Jesus.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r9.anchor: وقيل ؛ ظلمة البطن والرحم والمشيمة - نقل ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وعزاه ابن أبي الدنيا في كتاب القناعة إلى عيسى ابن مريم عليه السلام .

BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r10.claim: The demonstrative points to all the acts mentioned from the surah's beginning and testifies to God through every creature's speech or state; Lord means owner and nurturer through creation and provision.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r10.anchor: الذي جميع ما ذكر من أول السورة إلى هنا أفعاله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r11.claim: Since a nurturer need not be a sovereign, the argument concludes that God alone is deity and uniquely one.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r11.anchor: ولما كان المربي قد لا يكون ملكا قال نتيجة إلها , قال مثبتا له الإلهية على ما يقتضيه من الوحدانية

BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r12.claim: The final question challenges how people are diverted from exclusive devotion when all creatures are under God's command and power.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r12.anchor: ولما تكفل هذا السياق بوجوب الإخلاص في الإقبال عليه والإعراض عما سواه , لأن الكل تحت قهره

BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r13.claim: The passive form suggests people are overpowered in their conduct because they follow ruin and abandon unmistakable proofs; sound nature and reason originally prepare them for guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p421/r13.anchor: ونبه بالبناء للمفعول مع هذا على أنهم مقهورون في فعل ما هم عليه لأنهم تابعون للهلاك المحض

DURR-FULL:v7p211/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r3.claim: The single soul is Adam, and God created Adam's mate from one of his ribs.
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {خلقكم من نفس واحدة} يعني آدم {وخلق منها زوجها} خلقها من ضلع من أضلاعه

DURR-FULL:v7p211/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r4.claim: Creation in successive stages proceeds from a sperm-drop to a clot, lump, bones, flesh, and then hair growing in stages.
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r4.anchor: قال: نطفة ثم علقة ثم مضغة ثم عظاما ثم لحما ثم أنبت الشعر أطوارا

DURR-FULL:v7p211/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r5.claim: The three darknesses are the abdomen, womb, and placenta.
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r5.anchor: {في ظلمات ثلاث} قال: البطن والرحم والمشيمة

DURR-FULL:v7p211/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r6.claim: How then are you turned aside is like the question in 43:87.

DURR-FULL:v7p211/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r7.claim: The eight pairs of livestock are camels, cattle, sheep, and goats.
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {وأنزل لكم من الأنعام ثمانية أزواج} من الإبل والبقر والضان والمعز

DURR-FULL:v7p211/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r8.claim: Creation after creation means the sperm-drop and what follows it until the person's formation is complete.
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r8.anchor: وفي قوله {من بعد خلق} قال: نطفة ثم ما يتبعها حتى يتم خلقه

DURR-FULL:v7p211/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r9.claim: The three darknesses are the abdomen, womb, and placenta.
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r9.anchor: {في ظلمات ثلاث} قال: البطن والرحم والمشيمة

DURR-FULL:v7p211/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r10.claim: The stages include a clot, lump, and bones; the three darknesses are the abdomen, womb, and placenta.
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {خلقا من بعد خلق} قال: علقة ثم مضغة ثم عظاما {في ظلمات ثلاث} قال: ظلمة البطن وظلمة الرحم وظلمة المشيمة

DURR-FULL:v7p211/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r11.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r11.claim: The three darknesses are the abdomen, womb, and placenta.
DURR-FULL:v7p211/r11.anchor: عن أبي مالك رضي الله عنه في ظلمات ثلاث قال البطن والرحم والمشيمة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3248#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3248#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3248#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas describes fetal development from a clot to a morsel and bones, and identifies the three darknesses as the belly, womb, and placenta.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3248#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : خلقا من بعد خلق قال : علقة ثم مضغة ، ثم عظاما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r1.claim: “Creation after creation” means one distinct developmental stage after another; Ibn ʿĀshūr enumerates ten stages.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r1.anchor: وقوله : { خلقا من بعد خلق } أي طورا من الخلق بعد طور آخر يخالفه وهذه الأطوار عشرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r2.claim: Stage one is the nutfa: a white, round, mucous body without organs, wormlike and about five millimeters long.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r2.anchor: الأول : طور النطفة ، وهي جسم مخاطي مستدير أبيض خال من الأعضاء يشبه دودة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r3.claim: Stage two, the ʿalaqa, forms 33 days after implantation; it is about 13 millimeters, ant-sized, with a visible head and outlines of organs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r3.anchor: الثاني : طور العلقة ، وهي تتكون بعد ثلاثة وثلاثين يوما من وقت استقرار النطفة في الرحم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r4.claim: Stage three, the muḍgha, is a red piece about the size of a bee.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r4.anchor: الثالث : طور المضغة وهي قطعة حمراء في حجم النحلة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r5.claim: At two months the fetus is three centimeters long, its head half its remaining body; neck and face are indistinct and it remains red.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r5.anchor: الرابع : عند استكمال شهرين يصير طوله ثلاثة صانتميتر وحجم رأسه بمقدار نصف بقيته ولا يتميز عنقه ولا وجهه ويستمر احمراره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r6.claim: In month three it is 15 centimeters and 100 grams; forehead, nose, brows, and nails appear, while the skin remains red.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r6.anchor: الخامس : في الشهر الثالث يكون طوله خمسة عشر صانتيميترا ووزنه مائة غرام ويبدو رسم جبهته وأنفه وحواجبه وأظافره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r7.claim: In month four it reaches 20 centimeters; head down appears, abdominal organs exceed thoracic ones, and nails become clear toward month's end.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r7.anchor: السادس : في الشهر الرابع يصير طوله عشرين صانتيميترا ووزنه غرامات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r8.claim: By month six it is about 30 centimeters and 500 grams; its eyelids are closed and nails harden.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r8.anchor: السابع : في الشهر السادس يصير طوله نحو ثلاثين صنتيمترا ووزنه خمسمائة غرام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r9.claim: In month seven it is 38 centimeters; its skin reddens less and thickens, a greasy layer adheres, hair lengthens and lightens, and the skull bulges centrally.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r9.anchor: الثامن : في الشهر السابع يصير طوله ثمانية وثلاثين صنتيمترا ويقل احمرارا جلده ويتكاثف جلده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r10.claim: In month eight its girth grows faster than its length; it is about 40 centimeters and four pounds or more, with stronger movement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r10.anchor: التاسع : في الشهر الثامن يزيد غلظه أكثر من ازدياد طوله ويكون طوله نحو أربعين صنتيمترا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r11.claim: In month nine it is 50–60 centimeters and six to eight pounds; bones and hair mature, the head enlarges, and digestive, lung, and heart functions and fetal circulation begin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p333#2/r11.anchor: العاشر : في الشهر التاسع يصير طوله من خمسين إلى ستين صنتيمترا ووزنه من ستة إلى ثمانية أرطال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r1.claim: The three darknesses are the mother's abdomen, the womb, and the placenta.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r1.anchor: و ( الظلمات الثلاث ) : ظلمة بطن الأم ، وظلمة الرحم ، وظلمة المشيمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r2.claim: The placenta is a membrane formed with the fetus that surrounds and protects it and gives it an independent nutrient cycle from its mother.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r2.anchor: وهي غشاء من جلد يخلق مع الجنين محيطا به ليقيه وليكون به استقلاله مما ينجر إليه من الأغذية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r3.claim: The hidden surroundings of embryonic development point to God's encompassing knowledge and power reaching what is most concealed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r3.anchor: وفي ذكر هذه الظلمات تنبيه على إحاطة علم الله تعالى بالأشياء ونفوذ قدرته إليها في أشد ما تكون فيه من الخفاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r4.claim: Grammatically, khalqan is an absolute object specifying kind through “after creation”; “in three darknesses” modifies “He creates you.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r4.anchor: وانتصب { خلقا } على المفعولية المطلقة المبينة للنوعية باعتبار وصفه بأنه { من بعد خلق }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r5.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r5.claim: The majority read ummahātikum with ḍamma on hamza and fatḥa on mīm in both connected reading and pause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { أمهاتكم } بضم الهمزة وفتح الميم في حالي الوصل والوقف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r6.speaker: حمزة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r6.claim: Ḥamza reads the hamza and mīm of ummahātikum with kasra in connection, assimilating them to the preceding kasra and then to each other.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r6.anchor: وقرأه حمزة في حال الوصل بكسر الهمزة إتباعا لكسرة نون { بطون } وبكسر الميم إتباعا لكسر الهمزة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r7.speaker: الكسائي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r7.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads the mīm with kasra in connected reading while keeping the hamza open.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r7.anchor: وقرأه الكسائي بكسر الميم في حال الوصل مع فتح الهمزة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r8.claim: After describing God's control of the universe, beginning with the creation of the heavens and earth, the verse concludes that He alone controls all things and deserves worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r8.anchor: بعد أن أجري على اسم الله تعالى من الأخبار والصفات القاضية بأنه المتصرف في الأكوان كلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r9.claim: The demonstrative “that” singles out the bearer of the preceding attributes as uniquely deserving the predicate that follows; the sentence summarizes the preceding proofs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r9.anchor: أعقب ذلك باسم الإشارة للتنبيه على أنه حقيق بما يرد بعده من أجل تلك التصرفات والصفات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r10.claim: The demonstrative distinguishes the possessor of these attributes from others, leading into the ensuing statement, as in the parallel formulation in al-Baqara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r10.anchor: واسم الإشارة لتمييز صاحب تلك الصفات عن غيره تمييزا يفضي إلى ما يرد بعد اسم الإشارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r11.claim: The creator of people, livestock, and human stages is God, so none should be associated with Him; alleged gods did not create anything comparable.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r11.anchor: فلا تشركوا معه غيره إذ لم تبق شبهة تعذر أهل الشرك بشركهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r12.claim: Using God's proper name makes its referent unmistakable, clarifying for hearers treated as unaware that He performed these great acts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p334/r12.anchor: والإتيان باسمه العلم لإحضار المسمى في الأذهان باسم مختص زيادة في البيان

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p382#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p382#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p382#4/r1.claim: The eight pairs of livestock are eight kinds, those named by God in Sūrat al-Anʿām.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p382#4/r1.anchor: أي ثمانية أصناف، وهي التي ذكرها الله -عز ذكره- في سورة الأنعام

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p382#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p382#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p382#4/r2.claim: Creation in stages means a clinging form after a drop, then a lump after the clinging form.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p382#4/r2.anchor: أي علقة بعد نطفة ومضغة بعد علقة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p382#4/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p382#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p382#4/r3.claim: The three darknesses are said to be the placenta, womb, and abdomen.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p382#4/r3.anchor: يقال (5) : ظلمة المشيمة وظلمة الرحم وظلمة البطن.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r1.speaker: قتادة وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r1.claim: The “single soul” is Adam, according to Qatada and others; Ibn ʿAṭiyya also allows it to mean the human species.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r1.anchor: «النفس الواحدة» المرادة في الآية هي نفس آدم عليه السلام، قاله قتادة وغيره. ويحتمل أن يكون اسم الجنس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r2.claim: The surface sequence of “then” seems to place the creation of the spouse after the descendants, although that is not the actual order.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ثم جعل ظاهر اللفظ يقتضي أن جعل الزوجة من النفس هو بعد أن خلق الخلق منها، وليس الأمر كذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r3.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r3.claim: One group says “created you from one soul” refers to extracting descendants from Adam's back, before Eve was created.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r3.anchor: فقالت فرقة قوله: خلقكم من نفس واحدة هو أخذ الذرية من ظهر آدم وذلك شيء كان قبل خلق حواء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r4.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r4.claim: Another group takes “then” as ordering the account rather than the events: Eve had been made earlier, as the Abu Nuwas verse illustrates.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r4.anchor: وقالت فرقة: إنما هي لترتيب الأخبار لا لترتيب المعاني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r5.speaker: أبو النواس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r5.claim: Abu Nuwas's verse illustrates that a later-mentioned father and grandfather may have preceded the person in the stated sequence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r5.anchor: قل لمن ساد ثم ساد أبوه ... ثم قد ساد قبل ذلك جده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r6.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r6.claim: A third group understands the sequence as reporting what was already fixed in God's knowledge, so the certain future is narrated as settled before it came into being.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r6.anchor: وقالت فرقة قوله: خلقكم من نفس واحدة عبارة عن سبق ذلك في علم الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r7.claim: On the foreknowledge view, the events are ordered in the report although humanity's emergence from Adam actually followed the creation of Eve.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r7.anchor: فجاءت معان مترتبة وإن كان خروج خلق العالم من آدم إلى الوجود إنما يجيء بعد ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya favors the report that Eve was created from Adam's short rib, supported by the hadith that a woman was created from a rib and bending it breaks it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r8.anchor: وخلقت من ضلعه القصيري فيما روي، ويؤيد هذا الحديث الذي فيه أن المرأة خلقت من ضلع، فإن ذهبت تقيمه كسرته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r9.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r9.claim: Another group says Eve was created from leftover clay of Adam; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the rib account is sounder.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r9.anchor: وقالت فرقة: خلقت حواء من بقية طين آدم والأول أصح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r10.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r10.claim: One interpretation of “sent down” says the first animals were created in heaven and brought down to earth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r10.anchor: قيل معناه: أن المخلوق الأول من هذه الأنعام خلق في السماء وأهبط إلى الأرض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r11.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r11.claim: Another interpretation is that God's decree to create the animals came from Him; benefactions and rain are conventionally described as descending from heaven.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r11.anchor: وقالت فرقة: بل لما نزل الأمر بخلقه وإيجاده من عند الله، وكانت العادة في نعم الله ورحمته وأمطاره وغير ذلك أن يقال فيها إنها من السماء عبر عن هذه ب أنزل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r12.speaker: فرقة
