IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r12.claim: A third explanation links rainfall to grasses and plants, and plants to the animals' fattening and livelihood, so their provision is said to descend.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r12.anchor: لما كانت الأمطار تنزل وكانت الأعشاب والنبات عن المطر، وكانت هذه الأنعام عن النبات في سمنها ومعاشها، قال في هذه أنزل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r13.claim: The author introduces a rajaz poem as evidence for describing animal provision as descending through a gradual process.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r13.anchor: قال في هذه أنزل فهو على التدريج كما قال الراجز

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r14.claim: He explains the gradual account through the chain from rain to vegetation to the animals livelihood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p519#2/r14.anchor: وكانت هذه الأنعام عن النبات في سمنها ومعاشها، قال في هذه أنزل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r1.claim: The eight kinds are male-female pairs: sheep, goats, cattle, and camels.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r1.anchor: وجعلها ثمانية، لأن كل واحد فيه زوج للذكر من فرعه، وهي الضأن والمعز والبقر والإبل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says womb creation in successive stages includes development in Adam's and the fathers' backs before the mother's womb.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد، معناه: يخلقكم في البطون خلقا من بعد خلق آخر في ظهر آدم وظهور الآباء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r3.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة والسدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r3.claim: Mujahid, Ikrima, and al-Suddi take the successive creation in the womb to mean successive stages such as the clot and morsel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد وعكرمة والسدي: يخلقكم في البطون رتبا خلقا من بعد خلق على المضغة والعلقة وغير ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r4.speaker: عيسى بن عمر وطلحة بن مصرف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r4.claim: Isa ibn Umar and Talha ibn Musarrif assimilate qaf into kaf in “yakhluqukum” throughout the Qurʾan.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r4.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر وطلحة بن مصرف: يخلقكم بإدغام القاف في الكاف في جميع القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r5.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r5.claim: Most readers pronounce “mothers” with a damma on the hamza.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r6.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r6.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab pronounces the hamza in “mothers” with kasra; both pronunciations are dialects.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r6.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب: بكسرها وهي لغتان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r7.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r7.claim: One group identifies the three darknesses as the father's back, the mother's womb, and the placenta in the womb.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r7.anchor: قالت فرقة: الأولى هي ظهر الأب، ثم رحم الأم، ثم المشيمة في البطن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r8.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r8.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd identify them as the placenta, womb, and abdomen.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد: هي المشيمة والرحم والبطن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r9.claim: These signs alert people to the sole Creator who deserves worship and refute idol worship; the proofs make it clear that God is their Lord, so how can they turn away?
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p520/r9.anchor: وهذه الآيات كلها هي معتبر وتنبيه لهم على الخالق الصانع الذي لا يستحق العبادة غيره، وهذا كله في رد أمر الأصنام والإفساد لها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r1.claim: The single soul is Adam, and his spouse was created from him before his descendants were created.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r1.anchor: ﴿ خلقكم من نفس واحدة ﴾ يعني آدم ﴿ ثم جعل منها زوجها ﴾ أي قبل خلقكم جعل منها زوجها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r2.claim: The sequence marker then can precede a later-mentioned event that actually happened earlier, as in a statement contrasting what was given today with more given yesterday.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r3.speaker: غيره
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that the sequence simply announces afterward that God created Adam's spouse from him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r3.anchor: وقال غيره ثم أخبركم أنه خلق منها زوجها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r4.claim: God created the eight pairs of livestock; their details were given earlier in Sūrat al-Anʿām.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r4.anchor: ﴿ وأنزل لكم من الأنعام ﴾ أي خلق ﴿ ثمانية أزواج ﴾ وقد بيناها في سورة الأنعام 143

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r5.speaker: الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r5.claim: Creation after creation is the stages of a drop, clot, lump, bones, flesh, hair growth, and further changes until birth.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd instead understands the stages in the womb as following the person's creation in Adam's back.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r6.anchor: وقال ابن زيد خلقا في البطون من بعد خلقكم في ظهر آدم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r7.speaker: الجمهور وابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r7.claim: The three darknesses are the abdomen, womb, and placenta.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r7.anchor: ظلمة البطن وظلمة الرحم وظلمة المشيمة قاله الجمهور وابن زيد معهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r8.claim: An alternative set of three darknesses is the father's loins, the woman's abdomen, and the womb.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p163/r8.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة إنها ظلمة صلب الأب وظلمة بطن المرأة وظلمة الرحم

JISHUMI:v8p6038/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6038/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6038/r12.claim: Ināba is returning or turning back; the verb is anāba, yunību.
JISHUMI:v8p6038/r12.anchor: والإنابة: أصلها الرجوع، أناب ينيب إنابة، فهو منيب.

JISHUMI:v8p6038/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6038/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6038/r13.claim: Takhwīl is a substantial gift bestowed as a grant.
JISHUMI:v8p6038/r13.anchor: والتخويل: العطية العظيمة على جهة الهبة، وهي المتخولة

JISHUMI:v8p6038/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6038/r14.speaker: الحديث
JISHUMI:v8p6038/r14.claim: A cited hadith uses takhawwul for regularly tending to people through admonition.
JISHUMI:v8p6038/r14.anchor: ومنه الحديث: كان يتخولهم بالموعظة أي: يتعهدهم،

JISHUMI:v8p6038/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6038/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6038/r15.claim: The cited saying about Banū al-ʿĀṣ explains khawlan as servants treated as dependents or slaves.
JISHUMI:v8p6038/r15.anchor: إذا بلغ بنو العاص ثمانين رجلا اتخذوا مال الله دولا وعباد الله خولا، أيظنون العباد عبيدهم

JISHUMI:v8p6038/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6038/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6038/r16.claim: Disbelief is repaying blessing with denial; its opposite, gratitude, recognizes blessings, glorifies the giver, and obeys Him.
JISHUMI:v8p6038/r16.anchor: والكفر: مقابلة النعمة بالجحود، ونقيضه: الشكر، الاعتراف بالنعم وتعظيم المنعم وطاعته.

JISHUMI:v8p6038/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6038/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6038/r19.claim: The accusative khalqan is governed by the verb khalaqakum.

MUJAHID:v2p555#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p555#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p555#3/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the livestock of the eight pairs by listing camels, cattle, sheep, and goats.
MUJAHID:v2p555#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ وأنزل لكم من الأنعام ثمانية أزواج ﴾ يعني من الإبل والبقر والغنم والضأن والمعز

MUJAHID:v2p555#3/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p555#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p555#3/r2.claim: Mujahid describes formation as a drop, then a clot, then a lump, then bones, until creation is complete.
MUJAHID:v2p555#3/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ خلقا من بعد خلق ﴾ قال نطفة ثم علقة ثم مضغة ثم عظاما حتى يتم خلقه

MUJAHID:v2p555#3/r3.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p555#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p555#3/r3.claim: Mujahid says the three darknesses are the abdomen, womb, and placenta.
MUJAHID:v2p555#3/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ في ظلمات ثلاث ﴾ قال ظلمة البطن والرحم والمشيمة

MUQATIL:39:6-7/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:6-7/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:6-7/r1.claim: The single soul is Adam, and his mate is Eve.
MUQATIL:39:6-7/r1.anchor: يعنى آدم، عليه السلام { ثم جعل منها زوجها } يعنى حواء

MUQATIL:39:6-7/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:6-7/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:6-7/r2.claim: Sending down livestock means making them available, as sending down clothing and iron means making those things; the livestock are camels, cattle, and sheep.
MUQATIL:39:6-7/r2.anchor:
يعنى وجعل لكم من أمره مثل قوله فى الأعراف:
يابني آدم قد أنزلنا عليكم لباسا
[الأعراف: 26] يقول جعلنا،

MUQATIL:39:6-7/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:6-7/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:6-7/r3.claim: The eight pairs are kinds of livestock: four males and four females.
MUQATIL:39:6-7/r3.anchor: يعنى الإبل والبقر والغنم { ثمانية أزواج } يعنى أصناف، يعنى أربعة ذكور، وأربعة إناث

MUQATIL:39:6-7/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:6-7/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:6-7/r4.claim: Human development in the womb proceeds from a drop to a clot, a lump, bones, and then the spirit; the three darknesses are the belly, womb, and placenta.
MUQATIL:39:6-7/r4.anchor: يعنى نطفة، ثم علقة، ثم مضغة، ثم عظما، ثم الروح

MUQATIL:39:6-7/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:6-7/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:6-7/r5.claim: The Creator of these things is God, the sovereign Lord and only deity, so the question asks why people turn away from Him.
MUQATIL:39:6-7/r5.anchor: يقول: فمن أين تعدلون عنه إلى غيره.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r1.claim: The single soul is Adam; his spouse Eve was created from his rib.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r1.anchor: ﴿ خلقكم من نفس واحدة ﴾ أي آدم عليه السلام

NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r2.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r2.claim: One view says Adam’s descendants were drawn from his back like particles, then Eve was created afterward.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r2.anchor: قيل أخرج ذرية آدم من ظهره كالذر ثم خلق بعد ذلك حواء

NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r3.speaker: الحسن
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r3.claim: Al-Hasan explains that God made the livestock for people.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r3.anchor: ﴿ وأنزل لكم من الأنعام ﴾ أى جعل عن الحسن

NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r4.claim: Other explanations say livestock were created in Paradise with Adam and then sent down, or that they were sent down figuratively because they depend on plants and plants on sent-down water.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r4.anchor: أو خلقها فى الجنة مع آدم عليه السلام ثم أنزلها أو لأنها لا تعيش إلا بالنبات والنبات لا يقوم إلا بالماء وقد أنزل الماء فكأنه أنزلها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r5.claim: The eight pairs are male and female camels, cattle, sheep, and goats, as detailed in 6:143–144.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r5.anchor: ذكر وأنثى من الإبل والبقر والضأن والمعز كما بين فى سورة الأنعام

NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r6.claim: زوج names one member of a pair; when alone, it is an individual, fard or witr.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r6.anchor: والزوج اسم لواحد معه آخر فإذا انفرد فهو فرد ووتر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r7.claim: Human formation progresses from a sperm drop to a clot to a lump of flesh and then to complete formation.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r7.anchor: نطفة ثم علقة ثم مضغة ثم إلى تمام الخلق

NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r8.claim: The three darknesses are either the belly, womb, and placenta, or the backbone, belly, and womb.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r8.anchor: ظلمة البطن والرحم والمشيمة أو ظلمة الصلب والبطن والرحم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r9.claim: All these acts and possessions identify God as Lord and King; people should not turn from worshipping Him to worshipping another.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r9.anchor: فكيف يعدل بكم عن عبادته إلى عبادة غيره

NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r10.claim: The following verse clarifies that God is independent of people.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p48/r10.anchor: ثم بين أنه غنى عنهم بقوله

RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r2.claim: Human creation from one soul is evidence for a freely choosing Creator, a proof al-Razi says he has explained repeatedly.
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r2.anchor: ودلالة تكون الإنسان على الإله المختار قد سبق بيانها مرارا كثيرة

RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r3.claim: One answer says ثم may mark succession in discourse rather than event order, as when a speaker mentions today’s deed and then yesterday’s more remarkable deed.
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r3.anchor: أن كلمة ثم كما تجيء لبيان كون إحدى الواقعتين متأخرة عن الثانية ، فكذلك تجيء لبيان تأخر أحد الكلامين عن الآخر

RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r4.claim: A second answer supplies an omitted description: humanity was created from a soul created alone, after which its mate was made from it.
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r4.anchor: أن يكون التقدير خلقكم من نفس خلقت وحدها ثم جعل منها زوجها

RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r5.claim: A third answer says God first drew Adam’s descendants from his back like particles, then created Eve.
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r5.anchor: أخرج الله تعالى ذرية آدم من ظهره كالذر ثم خلق بعد ذلك حواء

RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r6.claim: Livestock are another proof of the Creator; the eight pairs are camels, cattle, sheep, and goats.
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r6.anchor: بوجود الحيوان عليه فقال : { وأنزل لكم من الانعام ثمانية أزواج } وهي الإبل والبقر والضأن والمعز

RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r7.claim: One explanation of “sent down” is that God’s decree and judgment descend from heaven because all events are written in the Preserved Tablet.
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r7.anchor: أن قضاء الله وتقديره وحكمه موصوف بالنزول من السماء لأجل أنه كتب في اللوح المحفوط كال كائن يكون

RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r8.claim: Another explanation links livestock’s being sent down to their dependence on plants, which depend on water and soil, with water descending from heaven.
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r8.anchor: شيئا من الحيوان لا يعيش إلا بالنبات والنبات لا يقوم إلا بالماء والتراب ، والماء ينزل من السماء فصار التقدير كأنه أنزلها

RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r9.claim: A third explanation says God created the livestock in Paradise and then sent them down to earth.
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r9.anchor: أنه تعالى خلقها في الجنة ثم أنزلها إلى الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r10.claim: Eight pairs means male and female of four livestock kinds; zawj names one member when paired with another and becomes an individual when alone.
RAZI-FULL:v26p213/r10.anchor: ثمانية أزواج } أي ذكر وأنثى من الإبل والبقر والضأن والمعز ، والزوج اسم لكل واحد معه آخر ، فإذا انفرد فهو فرد منه

RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r1.claim: The readings differ: Hamza kasras both alif and mīm in أمهاتكم; al-Kisāʾī kasras the hamza and opens the mīm; the others use a ḍamma on alif and fatḥa on mīm.
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة بكسر الألف والميم ، والكسائي بكسر الهمزة وفتح الميم ، والباقون أمهاتكم بضم الألف وفتح الميم

RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r2.claim: Livestock follows humanity because it is the noblest animal kind after humans; both are then described as developing in their mothers’ wombs.
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r2.anchor: خصها بالذكر لأنها أشرف الحيوانات بعد الإنسان ، ثم ذكر عقيب ذكرهما حالة مشتركة بين الإنسان وبين الأنعام وهي كونها مخلوقة في بطون أمهاتهم

RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r3.claim: “Creation after creation” refers to successive embryonic stages: clay essence, drop, clinging clot, morsel, bones, flesh, then a new creation.
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r3.anchor: خلقنا الإنسان من سلالة من طين * ثم جعلناه نطفة فى قرار مكين * ثم خلقنا النطفة علقة فخلقنا العلقة مضغة

RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r4.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r4.claim: One interpretation of the three darknesses is the abdomen, uterus, and placenta.
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r4.anchor: قيل : الظلمات الثلاث البطن والرحم والمشيمة

RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r5.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r5.claim: Another interpretation of the three darknesses is the loins, uterus, and abdomen.

RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r6.claim: The evidentiary force of these stages was discussed under God’s shaping people in wombs as He wills.
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r6.anchor: ووجه الاستدلال بهذه الحالات قد ذكرناه في قوله : { هو الذي يصوركم في الارحام كيف يشاء }

RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r7.claim: Calling God Lord identifies the one whose wondrous acts were recognized as the Creator.
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r7.anchor: ذالك * الله ربكم } أي : ذلكم الشيء الذي عرفتم عجائب أفعاله هو الله ربكم

RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r8.claim: By identifying God through His acts rather than body parts, the verse shows He is not composed of parts or organs and is transcendent beyond corporeality and place.
RAZI-FULL:v26p214/r8.anchor: ولو كان جسما مركبا من الأعضاء لكان تعريفه بتلك الأجزاء والأعضاء تعريفا للشيء بأجزاء حقيقته

STUDYQURAN:39:6/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r1.claim: Humanity's creation from one soul points to all human beings originating in Adam.
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r1.anchor: points to the origin of all human beings in Adam (IK)

STUDYQURAN:39:6/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r2.claim: Creating mates from human beings or their souls is a gift that should inspire awe and gratitude.
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r2.anchor: created for human beings mates from themselves (or“from their souls”) is a gift for which humanity should feel awe and gratitude

STUDYQURAN:39:6/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r3.claim: Sending down cattle means providing grazing livestock for human use, both for carrying burdens and for slaughter.
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r3.anchor: provided all manner of grazing livestock for human use, some for burden and some for slaughter (6:142).

STUDYQURAN:39:6/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r4.claim: The eight pairs are the male and female of sheep, goats, camels, and oxen.
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r4.anchor: The eight pairs refers to the male and female of sheep, goats, camel, and oxen; see 6:142c.

STUDYQURAN:39:6/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r5.claim: Creation after creation most likely refers to three stages of gestation described in 23:13–14, also compared with 22:5.
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r5.anchor: Creation after creation most likely alludes to the three stages of gestation mentioned in 23:13–14

STUDYQURAN:39:6/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r6.speaker: IK, JJ
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r6.claim: The threefold darkness alludes to the placenta, uterus, and belly surrounding the fetus.
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r6.anchor: the layers in which the fetus is wrapped: the placenta, the uterus, and the belly (IK, JJ)

STUDYQURAN:39:6/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r7.claim: The rhetorical question expresses amazement at turning from worship of the One responsible for all the realities in 39:5–6.
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r7.anchor: an expression of amazement asking how one could possibly turn away from the worship of the One who is responsible for all

STUDYQURAN:39:6/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r8.claim: The question challenges preferring worship of falsely attributed divine sons and daughters as intermediaries thought to bring people near to God.
STUDYQURAN:39:6/r8.anchor: preferring to worship the sons and daughters falsely ascribed to Him who it is claimed will bring one nigh in nearness unto God (v. 3).

TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r1.claim: The one soul is Adam; God made Eve his mate from one of Adam’s ribs.
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r1.anchor: ثم جعل من آدم زوجه حواء، وذلك أن الله خلقها من ضلع من أضلاعه

TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r2.claim: Qatadah identifies the single soul as Adam and says Eve was created from one of his ribs.
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {خلقكم من نفس واحدة} [النساء: 1] «يعني آدم، ثم خلق منها زوجها حواء، خلقها من ضلع من أضلاعه»

TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r3.claim: A report from the Prophet says God drew every soul destined to live until the Resurrection from Adam’s back before placing Adam in Paradise and creating Eve.
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r3.anchor: لأنه روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن الله لما خلق آدم مسح ظهره، فأخرج كل نسمة هي كائنة إلى يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r4.claim: One grammatical explanation takes “then” as the speaker’s narrative order: Arabs may mention the earlier event after the later one with thumma.
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r4.anchor: أن العرب ربما أخبر الرجل منهم عن رجل بفعلين، فيرد الأول منهما في المعنى بثم

TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r5.claim: Another grammatical explanation parses the phrase as creating you from a soul alone, then making that soul’s mate from it.
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r5.anchor: والوجه الآخر: أن يكون خلقه الزوج مردودا على واحدها، كأنه قيل: خلقكم من نفس وحدها ثم جعل منها زوجها

TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r6.speaker: الراجز
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r6.claim: The cited rajaz glosses كوحته as defeating or overcoming someone, supporting the alternative Arabic construction.
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r6.anchor: أعددته للخصم ذي التعدي … كوحته منك بدون الجهد

TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r7.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the first explanation: Adam’s descendants were brought from his loins before Eve was created, as reports from Companions also relate.
TAB-FULL:v20p161#2/r7.anchor: والقول الذي يقوله أهل العلم أولى بالصواب، وهو القول الأول الذي ذكرت أنه يقال: إن الله أخرج ذرية آدم من صلبه قبل أن يخلق حواء

TAB-FULL:v20p163/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p163/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p163/r1.claim: The eight livestock pairs are two each of camels, cattle, sheep, and goats, as also stated in 6:143.
TAB-FULL:v20p163/r1.anchor: من الإبل زوجين، ومن البقر زوجين، ومن الضأن اثنين، ومن المعز اثنين، كما قال جل ثناؤه: {ثمانية أزواج من الضأن اثنين ومن المعز اثنين} [الأنعام: 143]

TAB-FULL:v20p163/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p163/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p163/r2.claim: Mujahid says the eight pairs are camels, cattle, sheep, and goats.
TAB-FULL:v20p163/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {من الأنعام ثمانية أزواج} [الزمر: 6] قال: «من الإبل والبقر والضأن والمعز»

TAB-FULL:v20p163/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p163/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p163/r3.claim: Qatadah specifies two of each of the four livestock kinds: camels, cattle, sheep, and goats.
TAB-FULL:v20p163/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وأنزل لكم من الأنعام ثمانية أزواج} [الزمر: 6] «من الإبل اثنين، ومن البقر اثنين، ومن الضأن اثنين

TAB-FULL:v20p163/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p163/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v20p163/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak likewise counts two goats, two sheep, two cattle, and two camels.
TAB-FULL:v20p163/r4.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {وأنزل لكم من الأنعام ثمانية أزواج} [الزمر: 6] «يعني من المعز اثنين، ومن الضأن اثنين

TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r1.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r1.claim: Ikrimah lists the first stages as a drop, then a clot, then a lump.
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة، {يخلقكم في بطون أمهاتكم خلقا من بعد خلق} [الزمر: 6] قال: «نطفة، ثم علقة، ثم مضغة»

TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says the drop is followed by successive stages until formation is complete.
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {خلقا من بعد خلق} [الزمر: 6] قال: «نطفة، ثم ما يتبعها حتى تم خلقه»

TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r3.claim: Qatadah lists a drop, clot, lump, bones, flesh, and hair growth as the successive stages.
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {يخلقكم في بطون أمهاتكم خلقا من بعد خلق} [الزمر: 6] «نطفة، ثم علقة، ثم مضغة، ثم عظاما، ثم لحما، ثم أنبت الشعر، أطوار الخلق»

TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r4.claim: Ikrimah also names the clot, lump, and bones as stages after the initial creation.
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r4.anchor: عن سماك، عن عكرمة، في قوله: {يخلقكم في بطون أمهاتكم خلقا من بعد خلق} [الزمر: 6] قال: «يعني بخلق بعد الخلق، علقة، ثم مضغة، ثم عظاما»

TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi adds that after the drop, clot, lump, and bones, the spirit is breathed into the developing child.
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r5.anchor: عن السدي، في قوله: {يخلقكم في بطون أمهاتكم خلقا من بعد خلق} [الزمر: 6] قال: «يكونون نطفا، ثم يكونون علقا، ثم يكونون مضغا، ثم يكونون عظاما

TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak describes a drop, clot, and lump as the stages.
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r6.anchor: قال: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {في بطون أمهاتكم خلقا من بعد خلق} [الزمر: 6] «خلق نطفة، ثم علقة، ثم مضغة»

TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd offers a different reading: the creation in the womb follows the first creation of humanity in Adam’s back.
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد {يخلقكم في بطون أمهاتكم خلقا من بعد خلق} [الزمر: 6] قال: «خلقا في البطون من بعد الخلق الأول الذي خلقهم في ظهر آدم»

TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r8.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the womb-stage interpretation of Ikrimah, Mujahid, and those agreeing with them: the verse explicitly places successive creation in the womb amid three darknesses; he links this to 23:13.
TAB-FULL:v20p163#2/r8.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب، القول الذي قاله عكرمة ومجاهد، ومن قال في ذلك مثل قولهما

TAB-FULL:v20p166/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r1.claim: The three darknesses are the darkness of the belly, the womb, and the placenta.
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r1.anchor: عن سماك، عن عكرمة، {في ظلمات ثلاث} [الزمر: 6] قال: " الظلمات الثلاث: البطن، والرحم، والمشيمة "

TAB-FULL:v20p166/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r2.claim: Ikrimah identifies the three as belly, womb, and placenta.
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة، {في ظلمات ثلاث} [الزمر: 6] قال: " الظلمات الثلاث: البطن، والرحم، والمشيمة "

TAB-FULL:v20p166/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies them as the mother’s belly, womb, and placenta.
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {في ظلمات ثلاث} [الزمر: 6] قال: " يعني بالظلمات الثلاث: بطن أمه، والرحم، والمشيمة "

TAB-FULL:v20p166/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r4.claim: Mujahid names the belly, womb, and placenta.
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {في ظلمات ثلاث} [الزمر: 6] قال: «البطن، والرحم، والمشيمة»

TAB-FULL:v20p166/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r5.claim: Qatadah names the placenta, womb, and belly as the three darknesses.
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، {في ظلمات ثلاث} [الزمر: 6] «المشيمة، والرحم، والبطن»

TAB-FULL:v20p166/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r6.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r6.claim: Al-Suddi identifies darkness of the placenta, womb, and belly.
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r6.anchor: عن السدي، {في ظلمات ثلاث} [الزمر: 6] قال: «ظلمة المشيمة، وظلمة الرحم، وظلمة البطن»

TAB-FULL:v20p166/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd describes the nested order: the placenta is within the womb, and the womb within the belly.
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {في ظلمات ثلاث} [الزمر: 6] قال: «المشيمة في الرحم، والرحم في البطن»

TAB-FULL:v20p166/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r8.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak names womb, placenta, and belly, adding that the placenta is the afterbirth attached to an animal’s offspring at birth, called السلى.
TAB-FULL:v20p166/r8.anchor: قال: سمعت الضحاك، يقول، في قوله: {في ظلمات ثلاث} [الزمر: 6] : «الرحم، والمشيمة، والبطن، والمشيمة التي تكون على الولد إذا خرج، وهي من الدواب السلى»

TAB-FULL:v20p167#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p167#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p167#2/r1.claim: No deity deserves worship except God; the passage then challenges those who turn to worship something unable to harm or benefit them.

TAB-FULL:v20p167#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p167#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p167#2/r2.claim: The verse challenges people who turn from the Lord, whose attributes were just described, to worship something unable to harm or benefit them.
TAB-FULL:v20p167#2/r2.anchor: عن السدي، {فأنى تصرفون} [الزمر: 6] " قال للمشركين: أنى تصرف عقولكم عن هذا "

TAB-FULL:v20p167#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p167#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p167#2/r3.claim: Qatadah relates “how are you turned away?” to the wording “how are you deluded?” in 6:95.

TAB-FULL:v20p167#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p167#2/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p167#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says the question addresses the polytheists: how have their minds been turned away from this truth?
TAB-FULL:v20p167#2/r4.anchor: عن السدي، {فأنى تصرفون} [الزمر: 6] " قال للمشركين: أنى تصرف عقولكم عن هذا "

SAMIN-DURR:39:6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:6/r1.claim: ثم may mark temporal sequence: humanity was drawn from Adam like particles, and Eve was created later, according to a report.
SAMIN-DURR:39:6/r1.anchor: أنها على بابها من الترتيب بمهلة، وذلك أنه يروى أنه تعالى أخرجنا من ظهر آدم كالذر ثم خلق حواء بعد ذلك بزمان.

SAMIN-DURR:39:6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:6/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:6/r2.claim: ثم may be temporal while ordering Eve after the understood sense of واحدة: the original self was alone.
SAMIN-DURR:39:6/r2.anchor: الثاني: أنها على بابها أيضا ولكن لمدرك آخر: وهو أن يعطف بها ما بعدها على ما فهم من الصفة في قوله: " واحدة "

SAMIN-DURR:39:6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:6/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:6/r3.claim: ثم may order the report rather than existence in time, implying Eve had already been made from the self.
SAMIN-DURR:39:6/r3.anchor: الثالث: أنها للترتيب في الأخبار لا في الزمان الوجودي كأنه قيل: كان من أمرها قبل ذلك أن جعل منها زوجها.

SAMIN-DURR:39:6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:6/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:39:6/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes ثم as rank: Eve's creation from Adam's side is an exceptional, more striking sign than customary creation from Adam.
SAMIN-DURR:39:6/r4.anchor: فكانت أدخل في كونها آية وأجلب لعجب السامع، فعطفها ب " ثم " على الآية الأولى

SAMIN-DURR:39:6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:6/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:39:6/r5.claim: Here ثم marks the superior status of the second sign, not temporal delay.
SAMIN-DURR:39:6/r5.anchor: فهي من التراخي في الحال والمنزلة لا من التراخي في الوجود.

SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r1.claim: وأنزل لكم من الأنعام coordinates with خلقكم; literal descent is possible, on a report that the animals were created in Paradise and sent down.
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r1.anchor: عطف على " خلقكم " ، والإنزال يحتمل الحقيقة. يروى أنه خلقها في الجنة ثم أنزلها

SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r2.claim: Figuratively, animals are called sent down because they live on plants and water, and water descends from clouds; descent names a remote cause.
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r2.anchor: أنها لم تعش إلا بالنبات والماء، والنبات إنما يعيش بالماء، والماء ينزل من السحاب

SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r3.claim: Poetic examples illustrate this causal extension, including rain descending on a people's land.
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r3.anchor: وهو في الحقيقة يطلق على سبب السبب

SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r4.claim: Another figurative explanation invokes God's decrees and rulings, written in the Preserved Tablet and serving as a cause of the animals' creation.
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r4.anchor: أن قضاياه وأحكامه منزلة من السماء من حيث كتبها في اللوح المحفوظ، وهو أيضا سبب في إيجادها.

SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r5.claim: يخلقكم is an independent verbal clause, not a predicate of an omitted subject.
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r5.anchor: هذه الجملة استئنافية، ولا حاجة إلى جعلها خبر مبتدأ مضمر، بل استؤنفت للإخبار بجملة فعلية.

SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r6.claim: خلقاً is a verbal noun of يخلق; من بعد خلق may specify its type or attach to the verb while خلقاً serves only emphasis.
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r6.anchor: مصدر ل " يخلق " و { من بعد خلق } صفة له، فهو لبيان النوع

SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r7.claim: ظلمات attaches to the preceding خلق, not emphatic خلقاً; attachment to the verb is blocked by an identical preposition already governing it.
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r7.anchor: بخلق الذي قبله، ولا يجوز تعلقه ب " خلقا " المنصوب؛ لأنه مصدر مؤكد

SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r8.claim: Abu al-Baqa discusses attaching في ظلمات to خلقاً, then rules it out because the first مصدر is emphatic and cannot govern it.
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r8.anchor: فإنه قال: " و " في " متعلق به أي ب " خلقا " أو بخلق الثاني؛ لأن الأول مؤكد فلا يعمل "

SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r9.claim: في ظلمات may instead be an inclusion appositive of في بطون أمهاتكم; the repeated preposition is allowed and the intervening source phrase is not foreign to the same governor.
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#2/r9.anchor: فإن جعلت " في ظلمات " بدلا من { في بطون أمهاتكم } بدل اشتمال؛ لأن البطون مشتملة عليها

SAMIN-DURR:39:6#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#3/r1.claim: In ذلكم الله ربكم, الله may predicate of ذلكم with ربكم as adjective/appositive; alternatively الله is appositive and ربكم the predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#3/r1.anchor: ربكم " نعت لله أو بدل منه

SAMIN-DURR:39:6#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#3/r2.claim: له الملك may be independent, a successive predicate, or the predicate after الله and ربكم; it can also be a prepositional predicate with الملك as subject.
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#3/r2.anchor: قوله: " له الملك " يجوز أن يكون مستأنفا، ويجوز أن يكون خبرا بعد خبر

SAMIN-DURR:39:6#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#3/r3.claim: لا إله إلا هو may be independent or a successive predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:39:6#3/r3.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مستأنفا، وأن يكون خبرا بعد خبر.

TABATABAI:39:6-7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r1.claim: The womb passage explains how the previously mentioned humans and cattle are created; its address uses the rational form inclusively for non-rational creatures too.
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r1.anchor: بيان لكيفية خلق من تقدم ذكره من البشر والأنعام، وفي الخطاب تغليب أولي العقل على غيرهم

TABATABAI:39:6-7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r2.claim: Creation 'after creation' describes successive stages such as the drop, clinging clot, and lump of flesh.
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r2.anchor: والخلق من بعد الخلق التوالي والتوارد كخلق النطفة علقة وخلق العلقة مضغة وهكذا

TABATABAI:39:6-7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r3.claim: The three darknesses are the abdomen, womb, and placenta; al-Majma reports this interpretation from Abu Ja'far.
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r3.anchor: والظلمات الثلاث هي ظلمة البطن والرحم والمشيمة كما قيل ورواه في المجمع عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

TABATABAI:39:6-7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r4.claim: The alternative that the darknesses are the loins, womb, and placenta is mistaken: 'in your mothers' wombs' restricts them to women's bodies, not men's loins.
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r4.anchor: وهو خطأ فإن قوله { في بطون أمهاتكم } صريح في أن المراد بالظلمات الثلاث ما في بطون النساء دون أصلاب الرجال

TABATABAI:39:6-7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r5.claim: The creator and governor described in these verses is your sole Lord: as owner and manager of what he owns, he creates people, everything beyond them, and their operating order.
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r5.anchor: وإذ كان خالقا لكم ولكل شيء دونكم وللنظام الجاري فيكم فهو الذي يملككم ويدبر أمركم فهو ربكم لا غير

TABATABAI:39:6-7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r6.claim: God's ownership extends over all creatures in this world and the next; placing 'to him' first indicates exclusivity, and both ensuing clauses predicate further of 'that is God.'
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r6.anchor: وتقديم الظرف يفيد الحصر، والجملة خبر بعد خبر لقوله { ذلكم الله } كما أن قوله { لا إله إلا هو } كذلك

TABATABAI:39:6-7/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r7.claim: Exclusive divinity follows exclusive lordship because people worship a deity as a managing lord, from fear, hope, or gratitude.
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r7.anchor: لأن الإله إنما يعبد لأنه رب مدبر فيعبد إما خوفا منه أو رجاء فيه أو شكرا له

TABATABAI:39:6-7/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r8.claim: The question 'how are you turned away?' asks how people can leave worship of their creator, manager, and sovereign for another.
TABATABAI:39:6-7/r8.anchor: أي فكيف تصرفون عن عبادته إلى عبادة غيره وهو ربكم الذي خلقكم ودبر أمركم وهو المليك عليكم

ZAJJAJ:v4p345/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p345/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p345/r1.claim: The eight livestock pairs are male and female camels, cattle, sheep, and goats; each member of a pair is itself called a زوج.
ZAJJAJ:v4p345/r1.anchor:
من الإبل ذكرا وأنثى، ومن البقر ذكرا وأنثى ومن الضأن كذلك
ومن المعز ذكرا وأنثى

ZAJJAJ:v4p345/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p345/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p345/r2.claim: Creation proceeds from a drop, clot, morsel, bones, flesh covering the bones, then formation and the breathing of the spirit.
ZAJJAJ:v4p345/r2.anchor:
نطفا ثم علقا ثم مضغا ثم عظاما ثم تكسى العظام لحما، ثم تصور
وتنفخ فيها الروح

ZAJJAJ:v4p345/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p345/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p345/r3.claim: The three darknesses are the belly, womb, and placenta; another view identifies them as the loins, womb, and belly.
ZAJJAJ:v4p345/r3.anchor:
في البطن، والرحم، والمشيمة.
وقد قيل في الأصلاب والرحم والبطن

ZAJJAJ:v4p345/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p345/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p345/r4.claim: The one who manages creation in this way is God, unlike anything else.
ZAJJAJ:v4p345/r4.anchor: المعنى الذي دبر الخلق هذا التدبير ليس كمثله شيء

ZAJJAJ:v4p345/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p345/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p345/r5.claim: فأنى تصرفون asks how people can turn from the path of truth after this evidence for divine oneness, like the expression فأنى تؤفكون.
ZAJJAJ:v4p345/r5.anchor:
فمن أين تصرفون عن طريق الحق، مثل: (فأنى تؤفكون)
أي فكيف تعدلون عن الحق بعد هذا البيان الذي يدل على صحة التوحيد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:6-7/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:6-7/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:6-7/r2.claim: Humanity was created from Adam and his spouse Eve; livestock were sent down as eight pairs, explained in Surat al-An'am.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:6-7/r2.anchor: خلقكم من نفس واحدة } يعني: آدم عليه السلام { ثم جعل منها زوجها } حواء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:6-7/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:6-7/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:6-7/r3.claim: Human creation proceeds through sperm, then a clinging clot, then a lump, in three darknesses: the abdomen, womb, and placenta; this should turn people to God's worship.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:6-7/r3.anchor: أي: نطفة، ثم علقة، ثم مضغة { في ظلمات ثلاث } ظلمة البطن، وظلمة الرحم، وظلمة المشيمة

BURHAN:v3p307/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p307/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p307/r1.claim: The author rejects extending the address to livestock as needless strain: the point is God's power and care for people. He multiplies people through providence, reproduction, and livelihood, and makes livestock pairs for their continuance.
BURHAN:v3p307/r1.anchor: بأن جعل الخطاب شاملا للأنعام تكلف لا حاجة إليه لأن الغرض إظهار القدرة

ITQAN:v2p467#4/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p467#4/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p467#4/r1.claim: ثم ordinarily combines conjunction, sequence, and temporal delay; some Kufans and al-Akhfash allow it to be redundant, but Suyuti answers that the cited case has an omitted clause.
ITQAN:v2p467#4/r1.anchor: حرف يقتضي ثلاثة أمور التشريك في الحكم والترتيب والمهلة وفي كل خلاف أما التشريك فزعم الكوفيون والأخفش أنه قد يتخلف

ITQAN:v2p467#4/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p467#4/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p467#4/r2.claim: Against examples apparently reversing order or lacking a time gap, Suyuti says ثم orders reports rather than events; Ibn Hisham says that explains order but not delay.
ITQAN:v2p467#4/r2.anchor: ثم لترتيب الأخبار لا لترتيب الحكم

ITQAN:v1p118/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p118/r1.speaker: ابن أبي شيبة
ITQAN:v1p118/r1.claim: A report says the Qur’an descended whole to Gabriel on Laylat al-Qadr, was placed in the House of Might, then came down gradually.
ITQAN:v1p118/r1.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي شيبة في فضائل القرآن من وجه آخر عنه دفع إلى جبريل في ليلة القدر جملة واحدة

ITQAN:v1p118/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p118/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p118/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Qur’an descended whole on Laylat al-Qadr in Ramadan, then piecemeal over the months and days.
ITQAN:v1p118/r2.anchor: فقال ابن عباس إنه أنزل في رمضان ليلة القدر جملة واحدة ثم أنزل على مواقع النجوم

ITQAN:v1p118/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p118/r3.speaker: أبو شامة
ITQAN:v1p118/r3.claim: Abu Shama glosses رسلا as gradual delivery and مواقع النجوم as star settings, describing measured successive descent.
ITQAN:v1p118/r3.anchor: قال أبو شامة قوله رسلا أي رفقا وعلى مواقع النجوم أي على مثل مساقطها

ITQAN:v1p118/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p118/r4.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
ITQAN:v1p118/r4.claim: Al-Razi considers the annual needed portion descending from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven each Laylat al-Qadr, but leaves it undecided against the first account.
ITQAN:v1p118/r4.anchor: وهذا القول ذكره الإمام فخر الدين الرازي بحثا فقال يحتمل أنه كان ينزل في كل ليلة قدر ما يحتاج

ITQAN:v1p118/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p118/r5.speaker: ابن كثير
ITQAN:v1p118/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir says al-Qurtubi transmitted this possibility from Muqatil ibn Hayyan and reports consensus that the Qur’an descended whole to the House of Might in the lowest heaven.
ITQAN:v1p118/r5.anchor: قال ابن كثير وهذا الذي جعله احتمالا نقله القرطبي عن مقاتل بن حيان وحكى الإجماع

ITQAN:v1p118/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p118/r6.speaker: الحليمي والماوردي
ITQAN:v1p118/r6.claim: Al-Halimi and al-Mawardi also adopt Muqatil’s account of descent over successive Nights of Power.
ITQAN:v1p118/r6.anchor: وممن قال بقول مقاتل الحليمي والماوردي

ITQAN:v1p118/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p118/r7.speaker: ابن شهاب
ITQAN:v1p118/r7.claim: Ibn Shihab says the last Qur’anic verse connected with the Throne was the verse on debt.
ITQAN:v1p118/r7.anchor: ويوافقه قول ابن شهاب آخر القرآن عهدا بالعرش آية الدين

ITQAN:v1p118/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p118/r8.speaker: الشعبي
ITQAN:v1p118/r8.claim: Al-Sha‘bi’s third account is that revelation began on Laylat al-Qadr and continued piecemeal at different times afterward.
ITQAN:v1p118/r8.anchor: أنه ابتدئ إنزاله في ليلة القدر ثم نزل بعد ذلك منجما في أوقات مختلفة من سائر الأوقات وبه قال الشعبي

ITQAN:v1p118/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p118/r9.speaker: الماوردي
ITQAN:v1p118/r9.claim: Al-Mawardi’s fourth account has keepers send the whole Qur’an to Gabriel over twenty nights and Gabriel deliver it over twenty years; Ibn Hajar calls it strange.
ITQAN:v1p118/r9.anchor: حكى الماوردي قولا رابعا إنه نزل من اللوح المحفوظ جملة واحدة وأن الحفظة نجمته على جبريل

ITQAN:v1p118/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p118/r10.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v1p118/r10.claim: Ibn Hajar prefers the first account as sound and relied upon, and says Gabriel reviewed in Ramadan what had been revealed over the year.
ITQAN:v1p118/r10.anchor: قال ابن حجر في شرح البخاري والأول هو الصحيح المعتمد

DAMGHANI:v1p309/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p309/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p309/r9.claim: The three darknesses are three conditions in the womb; Jonah’s darknesses are night, water, and the whale; layered sea-darkness is glossed as heart, chest, and body.
DAMGHANI:v1p309/r9.anchor: الظلمات اي ثلاث ظلمات يعني ثلاث خصال قوله تعالى في سورة الزمر

DAMGHANI:v1p47/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p47/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p47/r6.claim: Among twenty listed referents for al-insān, the excerpt names Adam, his descendants, Hishām or al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, Qaraz ibn ʿAbd Allāh, Abū Jahl, al-Naḍr, Barsīṣā, Budayl, al-Akhnaṣ, Usayd, Kilda, and ʿUqba ibn al-Walīd.
DAMGHANI:v1p47/r6.anchor: آدم . ولد آدم . هشام بن المغيرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r1.claim: Inzāl is bringing an object down from a height; related words describe hardship descending and meeting in war.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r1.anchor: الإنزال : حط الشيء من العلو . والفاعل : منزل . والمفعول : منزل .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r2.claim: Nazīl means a guest; a cited line says the guest has the greatest rights.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r2.anchor: والنزيل : الضيف . وأنشدوا : نزيل القوم أعظمهم حقوقا … وحق الله في حق النزيل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r3.claim: Nazala can be used of pilgrimage; the source cites a line to illustrate the usage.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r3.anchor: أنازلة أسماء أم غير نازله … أبيني لنا يا أسم ما أنت فاعله

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r4.claim: Inzāl can mean speech or revelation, as in the boast of someone claiming to produce what God revealed.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r4.anchor: أحدها : القول . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة الأنعام : ﴿ قال سأنزل مثل ما أنزل الله ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r5.claim: A second sense is creation: provision of sustenance, livestock, and iron is described as sending them down.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r5.anchor: والثاني : الخلق . ومنه قوله تعالى في يونس : ﴿ قل أرأيتم ما أنزل الله لكم من رزق ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r6.claim: A third sense is bestowal or bountiful provision, as in God’s apportioning what He wills.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r6.anchor: والثالث : البسط ، ومنه قوله تعالى في حم عسق : ﴿ ولكن ينزل بقدر ما يشاء ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r7.claim: Inzāl also means actual sending down, exemplified by God sending rain after people despair.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p127/r7.anchor: والرابع : نفس الإنزال . ومنه قوله تعالى في [ حم ] عسق : ﴿ وهو الذي ينزل الغيث من بعد ما قنطوا

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r15.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r15.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r15.claim: Al-Anam uses أنشأكم من نفس واحدة, while al-Nisa, al-Araf, and al-Zumar use خلقكم من نفس واحدة; the choices suit each context and recurring vocabulary across those surahs.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r15.anchor: وقد راعى في هذا الاختيار السياق الذي وردت فيه الآية كما راعى تردد لفظ (الإنشاء) في الأنعام والنساء والأعراف والزمر

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#8/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#8/r4.speaker: درة التنزيل
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#8/r4.claim: The other lām passages occur amid accounts of the beginning of creation or of land and sea blessings, fitting motion toward its goal.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#8/r4.anchor: فالآيات التي تكتنفها في ذكر ابتداء خلق السموات والأرض وابتداء جري الكواكب وهي إذ ذاك تجري لبلوغ الغاية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1065/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1065/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1065/r1.claim: The single soul is Adam and the spouse made from him is Eve.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1065/r1.anchor: من المقصود بالنفس الواحدة؟ آدم عليه السلام

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1065/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1065/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1065/r2.claim: God brought Adam and Eve down to earth with the livestock pairs as provisions and necessities for life there, so they were not sent down without food.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1065/r2.anchor: أنزلهما إلى الأرض وأنزل معهما طعامهما مستلزمات الحياة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1065/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1065/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1065/r3.claim: The successive creation in mothers’ wombs refers to Adam and Eve’s descendants, not the first couple, whose creation was mentioned earlier.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1065/r3.anchor: هذا ليس آدم وحواء وإنما نحن وذكر خلق آدم وحواء في بداية السورة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1065/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1065/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1065/r4.claim: Al-Nahl first speaks of humanity’s creation and then livestock created for people; al-Zumar first mentions Adam and Eve, then their descendants and provisions.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1065/r4.anchor: هذا خلقنا نحن وليس آدم ثم ذكر بعدها

NASHR:v1p301/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p301/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p301/r2.claim: The text lists fourteen places of Ruways's optional assimilation: three in al-Baqara, then examples in al-Araf, al-Kahf, Maryam, Taha, al-Naml, al-Zumar, al-Rum, al-Shura, al-Najm, and al-Infitar.
NASHR:v1p301/r2.anchor: واختلف عنه أيضا في أربعة عشر حرفا وهي ثلاثة في البقرة فويل للذين يكتبون الكتاب بأيديهم

NASHR:v1p301/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p301/r9.speaker: طاهر بن غلبون وابن الفحام
NASHR:v1p301/r9.claim: Tahir ibn Ghalbun and Ibn al-Fahham report assimilation of anzala lakum in both locations; al-Mabhaj and al-Kifaya transmit it as well.
NASHR:v1p301/r9.anchor: وروى طاهر بن غلبون وابن الفحام إدغام أنزل لكم في الموضعين

NASHR:v1p302/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p302/r4.speaker: الباقون عن رويس
NASHR:v1p302/r4.claim: Other transmitters from Ruways show all these passages; both assimilation and clear pronunciation are sound transmissions from him.
NASHR:v1p302/r4.anchor: وروى الباقون عن رويس إظهار جميع ذلك، والوجهان عنه صحيحان
